title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses 66th Course of National Defence College
subtitle:
“National strategy must translate national purpose into action and national intent into national outcomes”: Vice-President

“India seeks to become a leading global power not to dominate others, but to ensure that no country dictates terms to us”: Vice-President

“Every Sovereign Nation Is Equal, Big or Small”: Vice-President

Vice-President Calls for Respect for National Sovereignty, Says No Country Should Encroach Upon Another’s Borders
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 12:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed participants of the 66th Course of the National Defence College (NDC), New Delhi, on the theme
“India’s Core Values, National Interests and National Objectives”.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the 66th Course of the National Defence College in New Delhi, emphasising that national strategy must translate national purpose into action and national intent into tangible outcomes. 

He stated that India’s ambition to emerge as a leading global power is not to dominate others, but to ensure that no country dictates terms to it. He underscored that every sovereign nation, big or small, deserves equal respect and that no country should encroach upon another’s territorial boundaries.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 12, 2026
Addressing 122 participants, including officers from the Indian Armed Forces, civil services, police and other government organisations, as well as 41 officers from friendly foreign countries, the Vice-President highlighted the importance of strategic thinking, integrated policymaking and international cooperation in addressing contemporary security challenges.
Emphasising that national values form the foundation of national identity and guide a country's engagement with the world, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan cited India’s civilisational philosophy of
‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’
(the world is one family). He referred to India’s Vaccine Maitri initiative during the COVID-19 pandemic, its role as a first responder during disasters and its leadership in international initiatives on climate action and disaster resilience as examples of these values in practice.
The Vice-President observed that India’s national interests flow from the constitutional values of sovereignty, democracy, secularism, justice, liberty, equality, fraternity and the unity and integrity of the nation. He underlined five broad priorities: safeguarding India’s sovereignty and territorial integrity; preserving its democratic, secular and federal character; advancing its strategic, political, economic and military objectives; ensuring a stable and secure environment for growth and human development; and contributing to international peace and stability.
Highlighting the increasingly interconnected nature of national security, Shri Radhakrishnan called for greater international cooperation to address challenges such as terrorism, cyber threats, pandemics, climate change and transnational crime. He noted that protecting national interests and advancing shared global interests are often mutually reinforcing objectives, requiring coordinated action, information sharing and mutual trust among nations.
Referring to
Viksit Bharat @ 2047
as a defining national objective, the Vice-President stressed the need to align long-term vision with available resources, sound policy choices and national priorities. He emphasised that national security encompasses the protection of India’s land, airspace, maritime interests and cyberspace, while creating conditions for sustained development and prosperity.
“India aims to become the most powerful nation in the world not to dominate others or dictate terms to others, but to ensure that no country dictates unethical terms to us,” the Vice-President said. He stressed that every nation’s sovereignty and self-respect must be respected and that countries must refrain from encroaching upon the territorial boundaries of others.
Calling for stronger engagement with the Global South, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted the principles of mutual respect, sovereign equality and shared development priorities. He urged countries to look beyond challenges and strengthen cooperation in technology, trade, connectivity, education, innovation and capacity building. He also emphasised that corruption remains a major challenge for the Global South and called for collective efforts to eradicate it.
The Vice-President urged the participants, as future strategic leaders, to adopt an integrated and forward-looking approach that transcends institutional and professional boundaries. He called upon them to understand the values that define their nations, identify the interests that must be protected, set clear objectives, prioritise them wisely and develop strategies to translate national intent into tangible outcomes.
Air Marshal Manish Kumar Gupta, Commandant, National Defence College, faculty members and participants of the 66th NDC Course were present on the occasion.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS FLORAL TRIBUTES TO SHRI SHIVRAJ V. PATIL
date:

                12 OCT 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to former Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Shivraj V. Patil, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan on his birth anniversary today.
Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament; former Members and other dignitaries also paid floral tributes to Shri Patil, on the occasion.
Secretary-General of Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh, and Secretary-General of Rajya Sabha, Shri P.C. Mody, also paid their tributes.
Born on 12 October 1935 in Chakur village of Latur district in Maharashtra, Shri Shivraj V. Patil dedicated his life to public service. After earning a Master's degree in Law from Bombay University, he began his legislative career in 1972 as a Member of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly, eventually serving as the Speaker from 1978 to 1979. He was first elected to the Seventh Lok Sabha in 1980 from the Latur parliamentary constituency, representing it across multiple consecutive Lok Sabha terms.
Shri Patil had the rare distinction of being unanimously elected as the Speaker of the Tenth Lok Sabha, an office he held from 10 July 1991 to 22 May 1996. He also played a pivotal role in the constitution of 17 Departmentally-related Standing Committees on 31 March 1993, a landmark initiative that strengthened Parliament’s role in ensuring greater accountability of the Executive. His initiatives further included the introduction of the MPLADS, computerisation of information services for Members, and live telecast of parliamentary proceedings.
Shri Patil passed away on 12 December 2025.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Felicitates Top-Performing Districts at PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana’s National Conference
subtitle:
Convergence of Schemes Transforms Ground Realities: Shri Chouhan Calls for Coordinated Action to Boost Farm Incomes

From Water Conservation to Natural Farming: District-Level Innovations Offer a Roadmap for Agricultural Growth

Shri Chouhan Calls for Higher Farm Credit in Eastern India, Pulses Cultivation in Rice Fallow Areas

No Goal Is Impossible with Determination: Shri Chouhan Urges Collectors to Accelerate Agricultural Development

District-Led Planning and Inter-Ministerial Coordination Key to Agricultural Growth: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
When policies are shaped by ground realities and all government departments work together in one direction, no district can be left behind in the race for development. This is the hallmark of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s model of good governance, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said on Monday. He was addressing the national conference on the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium in the Pusa campus, New Delhi. Addressing district collectors, scientists and senior policymakers from more than 50 districts across the country, Shri Chouhan extended his greetings on the auspicious occasion of Navratri and felicitated districts that had demonstrated outstanding performance. He urged officials to devote their full energy to realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a developed and prosperous India.
Districts at the Centre of Agricultural Planning
Emphasising the importance of localised planning, Chouhan said the framework for the PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana had been prepared by district collectors based on actual ground conditions rather than being drawn up in offices in Delhi. He stressed the need for regular monthly reviews, asking collectors to assess progress on their district agricultural action plans every month along with their teams. Where progress is slow, coordinated efforts across departments should be intensified to accelerate implementation. Highlighting the importance of inter-ministerial convergence, Shri Chouhan said farmers’ incomes could be increased manifold by bringing together the efforts of different ministries and institutions. These include the Ministry of Jal Shakti for water management; the Ministry of Food Processing Industries for processing and value addition; the Ministry of Cooperation and Farmer Producer Organisations for strengthening collective efforts; and the sectors of animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries, MSMEs and skill development. He also emphasised the need to strengthen the direct connection between agricultural research and farmers. Research conducted by nearly 16,000 scientists associated with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, along with the work of Krishi Vigyan Kendras, the Agricultural Technology Management Agency and agricultural universities, should reach farmers’ fields directly.
Focus on Low Productivity, Rice Fallow Areas and Credit Flow
Shri Chouhan said PMDDKY prioritises 100 districts that have lagged in agricultural productivity, have low cropping intensity or face inadequate institutional credit flow. He directed officials to promote pulses and oilseeds in rice fallow areas, where fields remain uncultivated after paddy harvesting, through a mission-mode approach. Expanding cultivation in these areas would help improve land utilisation and agricultural output. He also called for wider coverage of the Kisan Credit Card scheme and a faster flow of institutional credit, particularly in eastern India and underdeveloped districts. Farmers need access to capital to adopt advanced agricultural technologies and use better seeds and fertilisers, he said.
Chouhan Calls on Officials to Work with Determination
Motivating officials to pursue ambitious development goals, Shri Chouhan quoted the well-known lines: “Who says a hole cannot be made in the sky? Just throw a stone with conviction, my friends…” Encouraging district collectors to approach their responsibilities with determination, he shared the following lines:
If you wish, you can break mountains and hills;
If you wish, you can change the course of rivers;
If you wish, you can extract nectar from the soil;
If you wish, you can connect the earth with the sky!
Shri Chouhan said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had pledged from the ramparts of the Red Fort, during his third term, to work with three times the speed and strength. The agriculture and rural development machinery would put its full capabilities behind fulfilling this commitment, he said. Expressing confidence in the progress of the participating districts, Chouhan said competition would intensify ahead of the next review meeting, with several more districts expected to earn recognition for their outstanding work.
Districts Showcase Ground-Level Innovations and Success Stories
The conference recognised the best-performing districts for their exemplary work. District collectors also presented case studies highlighting innovative approaches to improving agricultural productivity, strengthening resilience and increasing farmers’ incomes.
Gadchiroli, Maharashtra: Through water conservation and drought management, the district transformed drought-affected areas into greener landscapes and achieved new milestones in agricultural production.
Alluri Sitharama Raju, Andhra Pradesh: In a low-rainfall region, the district promoted high-value horticultural crops requiring less water, resulting in a significant increase in farmers’ incomes.
Banka, Bihar: The district presented its Lilawaran Natural Farming Land Revival Model, which seeks to end dependence on chemical fertilisers and establish a new wave of natural farming.
Agricultural innovations undertaken by Kishtwar in Jammu and Kashmir, Korba in Chhattisgarh and Fazilka in Punjab were also widely appreciated.
The national conference was attended by Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary; Union Minister of State for Rural Development Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani; and Union Minister of State Krishan Pal Gurjar. Officials and representatives from the Ministries of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Jal Shakti and Rural Development also participated.
Senior officials present included Agriculture Secretary Atish Chandra; Secretary, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Naresh Pal Gangwar; Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Avinash Joshi; Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Dilip Kumar; Rural Development Secretary Rohit Kansal; Water Resources Secretary Archana Verma; and ICAR Director General and Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Dr M. L. Jat. Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Maninder Kaur Dwivedi was also present. Agriculture production commissioners and principal secretaries from various states, district collectors from more than 50 districts, and senior field officials from the Centre and state governments participated in the deliberations.

title: Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana Completes One Year
subtitle:
Gaya-Bihar, Nagaur-Rajasthan and Umaria- Madhya Pradesh, Recognised as Best-Performing Districts

The ultimate measure of PMDDKY’s success would be the meaningful difference it makes to the lives of farmers: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Chouhan

Union Minister Calls for Outcome-Oriented Implementation of PMDDKY in its Second Year
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY) completed one year of implementation on 11th October 2026, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, organised an event today to mark the occasion at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), PUSA, New Delhi. The event was attended by  Union Ministers, Secretaries of Central Ministries/Departments, Central Nodal Officers under PMDDKY, senior officers of the Central Government, and more than 370 delegates from the states including District Collectors, district-level functionaries, agricultural scientists and progressive farmers of DDKY districts.
Addressing the gathering Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that the first year had focused on establishing strong foundations, while the coming year must be dedicated to delivering visible and measurable outcomes on the ground. He highlighted the importance of improving agricultural productivity, increasing cropping intensity, strengthening irrigation and water management, facilitating access to agricultural credit, promoting high-value agriculture, improving post-harvest infrastructure and enhancing farmers’ incomes.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasised that the ultimate measure of PMDDKY’s success would be the meaningful difference it makes to the lives of farmers. He called upon all stakeholders to strengthen coordination, accelerate implementation and focus on measurable improvements in agricultural outcomes and sustainable farm incomes. The participation of Allied Ministries/Departments reflected the importance of a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to agricultural development.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan reaffirmed the Government of India’s commitment to working with State Governments, district administrations, scientific institutions and farmers to translate district action plans into tangible results. The coming year will focus on scaling up successful interventions and improving outcomes across all identified districts, with the overarching vision of making all 100 PMDDKY districts truly “Dhan-Dhaanya” — rich in grain and rich in prosperity.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also emphasised that the Khet Bachao Abhiyan, scheduled to be organised across all States from 22 October to 30 November 2026, aims to promote soil health through the balanced and judicious use of fertilisers. The Minister encouraged all State Governments and concerned authorities to actively participate in the campaign and ensure its successful implementation. He highlighted the importance of adopting sustainable agricultural practices to maintain soil fertility, protect the environment, and preserve natural resources for future generations.
In his welcome address, the Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, highlighted the district-centric approach of the scheme, under which action plans are prepared by districts in accordance with their soil conditions, rainfall, cropping patterns, water availability, infrastructure and the needs of their farming communities. He acknowledged the contribution of State Governments, District Collectors, District Nodal Officers, Central Nodal Officers, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) scientists and field functionaries in implementing the scheme. He also underscored the importance of the District Dhan-Dhaanya Samitis in coordinating planning and implementation. The scheme monitors district performance against 121 indicators through a dedicated dashboard, with monthly rankings encouraging transparency and healthy competition among districts.
As part of the programme, representatives of three PMDDKY districts shared their experiences and innovative initiatives. Gadchiroli district presented its work on
water conservation and drought resilience
, Alluri Sitharama Raju district highlighted initiatives for the
promotion of high-value horticulture
, and Banka district showcased the
Lilawaran Natural Farming Land Revival Model
. The presentations demonstrated how locally tailored interventions, supported by convergence and farmers’ participation, can address agricultural challenges and generate replicable solutions.

title: Coal stocks at power plants remain stable above 18 MT; depletion thins out in October 2026 as coal supplies strengthen
subtitle: Ministry of Coal acknowledges the continued support and professional commitment of Indian Railways in facilitating the efficient movement of coal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 10:00AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The coal stocks at domestic coal-based power plants have remained stable above 18 million tonnes (MT) since 29 September 2026. Stock was 18.932 MT on 29 September and is at 18.205 MT on 10 October 2026. The stabilisation reflects coal supplies keeping pace with daily consumption at power plants and the supply to the plants with critical stocks is being closely monitored, with requirement-based redistribution of coal to vulnerable stations to ensure adequate supplies and uninterrupted power generation.
Stock accretion was recorded on two dates in October 2026:
2 October 2026: 0.024 MT
10 October 2026: 0.017 MT
The pace of depletion has eased considerably in October compared to September:
In September 2026, stock declined by about 7.28 MT over the month, an average of about 0.24 MT per day.
In the first ten days of October 2026, stock declined by only about 0.56 MT in total, an average of about 0.06 MT per day.
Higher rake loading has driven this improvement. Rakes loaded to the power sector averaged 469 rakes per day in October 2026 (1–10 October), against 426 rakes per day in September 2026, an increase of about 10%. Daily rake loading in October has ranged between 447 and 482 rakes.
As a result, actual coal supply to the power sector averaged
2.49 MT per day in October 2026
, against 2.21 MT per day in September 2026. The actual coal supply in October 26 (till 10.10.2026) is higher than supply plan of 2.37 MT per day, and supply exceeded the plan on nine of the ten days.
The Ministry continues to work in close coordination with Coal India Limited (CIL), SCCL, the Ministry of Railways and power utilities to ensure sustained coal evacuation and supply, thereby maintaining adequate coal stocks at thermal power plants. The Ministry of Coal duly acknowledges and appreciates the continued support and professional commitment of Indian Railways in facilitating the efficient movement of coal.

title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Doubling India-UK Bilateral Trade by 2030
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Highlights Complementary Strengths of India and UK, Calls for Diversifying Trade and Exploring New Export Opportunities

Shri Goyal Identifies Five Key Areas for India-UK Cooperation, Including Clean Energy and Advanced Manufacturing

Rt Hon Jonathan Reynolds MP, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, UK, Stresses Effective Implementation of CETA to Boost India-UK Trade

Union Minister of State Shri Jitin Prasada Highlights Technology Collaboration as Next Frontier of India-UK Economic Relations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal has called upon businesses in India and the United Kingdom to translate the opportunities created by the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) into expanded trade, investment, partnerships and job creation. Addressing the JETCO Business Plenary under the 16th Session of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO), he said the two countries should aim to double bilateral trade by 2030 and make the India-UK Vision 2035 a framework for greater economic ambition and cooperation.
Shri Goyal said CETA marks a major milestone in the economic partnership between the two countries, providing zero-duty access in the United Kingdom market for most Indian exports while opening up significant opportunities for UK exporters across sectors. The agreement has also opened up new opportunities in services. He added that the Social Security Double Contribution Convention could further benefit both economies through the supply of services at competitive prices and improved profitability.
Emphasising the need to convert the agreement into tangible business outcomes, the Minister said, “This agreement opens the doors businesses have to walk through.” He called for businesses to make the most of the opportunities available under CETA and said that 2030 should not merely mark the end of the decade but the beginning of much greater ambition between the two countries. Referring to the approximately 1,500 days remaining until the end of 2030, he urged businesses to work towards achieving the shared ambition of doubling bilateral trade.
Continuing his address Shri Goyal said India and the UK were complementary economies with considerable potential to expand existing trade, develop new export opportunities and diversify the range of products exchanged. India brings scale, a deepening manufacturing base, world-class digital public infrastructure and the youngest talent pool available anywhere in the world, while the UK brings strengths in research, design, advanced technologies and one of the world's leading financial centres.
Highlighting the existing trade complementarities, the Minister noted that India was a major exporter of smartphones, pharmaceutical products, jewellery, textiles, leather goods, rice and certain agricultural products, iron and non-alloy steel, machinery parts and auto components. On the UK side, he identified potential in the supply of products across the petroleum value chain, technology products in electronics and electrical equipment, medicaments, motor cars and Scotch whisky. He said the wide-ranging CETA had opened up numerous opportunities to expand trade, encourage new exporters and introduce new product lines.
The Minister also highlighted the significant potential for investments in both directions. He noted that several Indian companies had invested substantially in core sectors in the UK, while prominent UK companies had invested in India. He said the Ministry of Commerce and Industry would be willing to cooperate in expanding existing frameworks, enhancing mutual recognition in different areas and supporting both economies to move forward at a faster pace.
Setting out five priority areas for India-UK cooperation, Shri Goyal said infrastructure and clean energy offered opportunities in project development, renewable energy, transmission lines and utility financing to support sustainable growth in both countries.
The second area was advanced manufacturing and resilient supply chains, particularly in electric vehicles, batteries, electronics and precision engineering. He said cooperation should help build competitive manufacturing ecosystems, strengthen supply-chain resilience and enhance confidence between the two trusted partners.
The third priority was technology and innovation. He called for stronger links between educational and research institutions, technology companies and start-ups, alongside greater research and development cooperation. He highlighted opportunities for collaboration in semiconductors, quantum computing and artificial intelligence.
The fourth area was financial services, where he called for greater collaboration between the City of London and GIFT City in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. He identified fintech, insurance, cross-border payments, transition finance and trade finance as areas for cooperation, adding that the two financial centres should work towards becoming a connected pathway to greater progress and prosperity.
The fifth area was healthcare and consumer sectors. Shri Goyal highlighted opportunities in generic pharmaceuticals on the Indian side and branded and innovative pharmaceutical products on the UK side, as well as diagnostics, food processing and consumer goods. He said India's affordability and Britain's strengths in discovery could together become a force multiplier. He added that skills and training across all five areas would be important in expanding business potential, as capital could move quickly across borders but capabilities took time to develop. He stressed the need to invest in mutual understanding and capacity-building to expand trade between the two countries.
Calling for practical support to help businesses benefit from CETA, Shri Goyal emphasised the need to make tariff schedules, rules of origin and documentation requirements accessible through clear instructions. He called for supporting material in plain language and, in the Indian context, regional languages, so that businesses of different sizes and from different regions could navigate the agreement effectively. Referring to a unit in Tirupur in southern India and an engineering firm in the Midlands, he said accessible guidance, including in Tamil where relevant, would help businesses make use of the agreement.
The Minister said one measure of success would be the number of new exporters entering the UK market with new products. He called for greater engagement between businesses on both sides through regular sectoral round tables, sectoral delegations and participation in exhibitions at scale, including as partner countries, to demonstrate the commitment of both countries to implementing the free trade agreement.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal called for translating the promise of India-UK Vision 2035 into progress on the ground, guided by the principle that when nations grow together, their people prosper together.
Addressing the session Rt Hon Jonathan Reynolds MP, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade of the United Kingdom, said that the conclusion of the India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) marked the beginning of a sustained and practical dialogue between governments and businesses on both sides. He noted that the government-to-government JETCO meeting had concluded ahead of the business dialogue, with the launch of committees and working groups and a joint review of utilisation to address business feedback, resolve implementation issues and improve delivery. With CETA having been in force for almost 100 days, he said there were encouraging signs of businesses in both countries beginning to use the agreement and explore new opportunities across advanced manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences, technology, services and creative industries. He emphasised that the agreement’s success would depend on businesses using it to expand exports, investment and partnerships.
Mr. Reynolds stressed the need for practical support to help businesses, particularly MSMEs and first-time exporters, understand tariff reductions, rules of origin, customs procedures, regulatory requirements and procurement opportunities. He underlined the importance of frank and constructive feedback from businesses to identify implementation challenges and areas where further government action could facilitate trade and investment. He said that business feedback would be taken up through CETA’s utilisation review, committees and working groups, adding that the agreement was a starting point for further expansion of India–UK trade relations. He called for translating the commitment to trade and cooperation into tangible outcomes, including contracts, investments, commercialisation of technologies and job creation in both countries, and reaffirmed the importance of keeping businesses at the centre of implementation.
Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada in his address said that sustained engagement between India and the UK business communities through business missions and exchanges between industrial associations would help companies identify prospective partners, explore opportunities and strengthen commercial ties across regions and enterprises of different sizes. He highlighted technological collaboration as the next frontier of India–UK economic relations, particularly in artificial intelligence, semiconductors and data centres. He noted that the UK’s strengths in research and development, combined with India’s engineering talent, digital market and ability to deploy technologies at scale, offered opportunities for collaboration. Referring to the Technology Security Initiative agreed in 2024, he said both countries could work towards developing trusted and affordable technologies for global markets. He emphasised that continued government–industry engagement would strengthen business confidence and called for measuring progress at the next JETCO through partnerships signed, factories opened and jobs created.
This was the first JETCO session following the signing and entry into force of the India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) on 15 July 2026. The Ministers reviewed early business uptake of CETA, bilateral trade and investment developments, and priorities for the year ahead.
The JETCO coincided with the visit of seven mayors and a combined authority leader from the North of England. It supported a broader programme of engagement involving government, business, universities, innovators and regional leaders from both countries, including parallel visits by the UK's Secretaries of State for Scotland and for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
Both sides undertook a Joint Utilisation Review of CETA and welcomed the speed with which businesses in both countries have used the agreement. The Ministers also welcomed the establishment of sub-committees and working groups under CETA and exchange of contact points for these sub-committees and working groups. The Ministers agreed that the committees will engage and develop a practical forward roadmap identifying the priority areas and issues on which they will work.
The UK India Business Council (UKIBC), the strategic and knowledge partner to the Great North delegation, is supporting a first-of-its-kind mayoral mission to India bringing together leaders from five Combined Authorities across the North of England.
UKIBC has provided the delegation with strategic and market insights on India, identified bilateral opportunities across priority sectors, and facilitated engagement with Indian industry and government. The mission forms part of UKIBC's wider work with Northern regions, which includes identifying each region's strongest proposition in India, developing market strategies and engagement plans, and building long-term partnerships with Indian businesses and institutions. These efforts aim to translate intent into practical programmes on the ground.

title: Joint Statement of the 16th Meeting of the India–UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
We, Shri Piyush Ved Prakash Goyal, Honourable Minister of Commerce and Industry of India, and the Rt Hon Jonathan Reynolds MP, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade of the United Kingdom, met today in New Delhi for the 16th meeting of the India–UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO).
This is the first JETCO since negotiations started in January 2022 for the India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). We celebrated this landmark agreement that is already delivering for businesses in both countries. We were clear that the CETA marks the beginning, not the end, of our shared ambition: it is the foundation for a deeper and broader economic partnership in the years ahead.
The JETCO assumed greater significance as it coincided with the visit of seven mayors and a combined authority leader from the North of England. It supported a broader programme of engagement involving government, business, universities, innovators and regional leaders from both countries, including parallel visits by the UK's Secretaries of State for Scotland and for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
We welcomed the delegation from the North of England, and recognised the contribution that states, regions and cities make to strengthening trade, investment, innovation and people-to-people links.
Our discussions reflected the growing ambition and breadth of the India–UK partnership. We discussed the global economic outlook and progress since CETA entered into force, and agreed priorities for the year ahead.
Locking in benefits
We welcomed the speed with which businesses in both countries have used the agreement. On the day it entered into force, Indian exporters sent more than 50 consignments to the UK, including electronics such as smartphones, electrical and mechanical machinery including turbojets, gold jewellery, ready-made garments, woollen yarn, tea and coffee. The shipment of Joha rice from Assam to the UK, makes it the first export of this distinctive regional variety to the UK. The first Certificates of Origin under the CETA were also issued through India’s eCoO 2.0 platform on a self-certification basis, facilitating exporters’ access to preferential treatment from the outset. The first tariff-free Scottish salmon reached India from the UK within a fortnight, with several thousand kilos exported since. Scotch whisky has also entered the Indian market under reduced tariffs, and the first cars exported under the tariff-rate quota have cleared customs and been imported into India.
We agreed that we will exchange data annually starting one year after the date of entry into force of the CETA on how businesses are using the agreement. This will include data on how often businesses claim CETA’s lower tariffs, alongside business feedback on what is working well and where further support is needed. This will give us a shared picture of priorities and show where we can help more companies, especially small and medium-sized businesses, take advantage of the agreement.
We also agreed a plan to ensure the continued smooth operation of CETA, including establishing its committees and working groups and confirming government-to-government contact points for every part of the agreement. We welcomed the close cooperation that has helped in the early resolution of issues and asked officials to address challenges that may arise quickly.
Delivering more for business
We agreed to build on the CETA and deepen cooperation across services, innovation, government procurement, science and technology, and gender, with greater business to business engagement and enhanced regional partnerships, so that the agreement delivers growth in every part of both countries.
We welcomed today's meeting of the India–UK Science and Innovation Council and the Innovation Roundtable. Such engagements connect businesses, investors and researchers and help in the faster commercialisation of new technologies.
We welcomed the strong industry engagement accompanying the 16th JETCO and recognised the value of continued business-to-business interactions, sectoral roundtables and stakeholder engagement in identifying opportunities and implementation challenges.
We agreed to continue drawing on feedback from businesses, industry associations, export promotion bodies and other stakeholders to identify and address CETA implementation issues.
We agreed that visits of high-level delegations should continue to maintain the momentum generated by this JETCO meeting.
Next JETCO Meeting
We agreed that the 17th JETCO will take place in the United Kingdom in 2027.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Emphasises a Twin-Track Approach of Global Technologies and Employment Generation
subtitle:
Union Minister addresses ‘Dilli Dialogue: Policies for a Future-Ready India’

India to Become Car Manufacturing Hub of the World: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, emphasised a twin-track approach of engaging with the world’s best technologies and identifying areas with significant job and business potential.
Addressing the ‘Dilli Dialogue: Policies for a Future-Ready India’ in New Delhi, today, he highlighted the importance of creating opportunities for businesses, startups and young people. The Minister said, “We want to be a part of the global marketplace. Providing opportunities for people, providing opportunities for jobs, for our startups, for our youth to come up with newer ideas.”
Shri Goyal highlighted India’s expanding engagement with global markets through Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), emphasising the opportunities these agreements create for Indian businesses and youth. He said that India’s partnerships with developed economies could benefit both sides, with India offering strengths in textiles, footwear, agriculture and food processing while gaining access to advanced technologies and high-quality electronic equipment.
Emphasising India’s approach to global engagement and self-reliance, Shri Goyal said, “We are not closing the doors of India to the world. We are, in fact, opening them wider.”
Shri Piyush Goyal, also emphasised the importance of setting ambitious targets for India’s economic growth and exports while speaking at the event, Shri Goyal referred to the trillion-dollar export target and expressed confidence in India’s ability to achieve it and highlighted the importance of pursuing ambitious national goals as part of the country’s journey towards ‘Viksit Bharat 2047.’
The Minister said that India’s ambition of becoming a developed nation by 2047 is supported by a roadmap identifying sectors that will contribute to the country’s growth. He highlighted the rising demand for goods and services among India’s 1.4 billion people and said that growing imports also indicate opportunities for domestic industry and international investors. He noted that increasing demand for electronics and white goods could encourage investment in domestic manufacturing, including semiconductor factories.
Shri Goyal identified tourism as a sector with substantial potential to generate employment and create new business opportunities. He said that artificial intelligence could improve the efficiency of tourism promotion, while human experiences would remain central to the sector. He stated, “AI can only add to the efficiency of promoting tourism. But otherwise, human experiences will always be AI proof.”
He also highlighted India’s culinary heritage and regional diversity, referring to the potential of Indian food traditions and products such as filter coffee, rasam, idli and dosa.
Shri Goyal also highlighted India’s demographic advantage, noting that its young population offers opportunities at a time when many economies are experiencing ageing populations. He referred to the demand for Indian workers in countries such as Germany and Japan and highlighted the potential for Indian professionals to contribute to international markets. Shri Goyal also highlighted the trust placed in Indian workers internationally, stating that Indians are respected for their honesty and their commitment to caring for others.
Shri Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India would emerge as a global hub for car manufacturing, stating that international automobile manufacturers would increasingly manufacture in India as market demand reaches a viable scale. Referring to the quotas permitted for car imports from the United Kingdom and the European Union, Shri Goyal explained that these largely covered expensive cars, while the lower-priced segment had not been opened. Citing the examples of luxury automobile manufacturers establishing manufacturing plants in Pune after initially testing the Indian market, Shri Goyal highlighted India’s potential to attract global automobile manufacturers and strengthen its position in global car manufacturing.
Emphasising the importance of quality in strengthening India’s global competitiveness, the Minister called for collective efforts by policymakers, industry stakeholders and institutions, including the Bureau of Indian Standards and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, to improve quality standards.
Shri Goyal concluded by emphasising that if India adopts and practises world-class quality standards, no power on earth can stop it and the world is India’s to capture.

The Indian Telecom Services Performance Indicators
April–June 2026
Executive Summary
Total number of Internet subscribers increased from 1092.79 million at the end of March 2026 to 1114.17 million at the end of June 2026, registering a quarterly rate of growth of 96%. Out of 1114.17 million Internet subscribers, number of Wired Internet subscribers are 47.73 million and number of Wireless Internet subscribers are 1066.43 million.
Composition of Internet Subscription
The Internet subscriber base is comprised of Broadband Internet subscriber base of 1087.50 million and Narrowband Internet subscriber base of 26.67 million.
The broadband Internet subscriber base increased by 2.03% from 1065.88 million at the end of March 2026 to 1087.50 million at the end of June 2026. The narrowband Internet subscriber base decreased by 0.89% from 26.91 million at the end of March 2026 to 26.67 million at the end of June 2026.
Wireline subscribers decreased from 48.25 million at the end of March 2026 to 47.82 million at the end of June 2026 with a quarterly rate of decline 0.88%. On Y-O-Y basis, wireline subscriptions increased by 0.71% at the end of quarter ending June 2026.
Wireline Tele-density decreased from 3.38% at the end of March 2026 to 3.35% at the end of June 2026 with quarterly rate of decline 1.06%.
Monthly Average Revenue per User (ARPU)  for wireless service increased by 1.19%, from ₹184.91 in quarter ending March 2026 to ₹187.12 in quarter ending June 2026. On Y-O-Y basis, monthly ARPU for wireless service increased by 3.11% in this quarter.
The ARPU per month for the pre-paid segment is ₹200.72 and the ARPU per month for the post-paid segment is ₹114.26 for quarter ending June 2026.
On an all-India average, the overall MOU per month decreased by 2.65% from 959 in quarter ending March 2026 to 933 in quarter ending June 2026.
Prepaid MOU per subscriber is 1055 and Postpaid MOU per subscriber per month is 279 in quarter ending June 2026.
Average revenue realization per GB for wireless data usage decreased from ₹7.51 in quarter ending March 2026 to ₹7.13 in quarter ending June 2026 with quarterly rate of decline of 5.07%.
Number of wireless (Mobile) data subscribers has increased from 1026.75 million at the end of March 2026 to 1045.55 million at the end of June 2026 with quarterly rate of growth of 1.86%.  Further, total volume of wireless (mobile) data usage also increased from 77,953 PB during quarter ending March 2026 to 84,424 PB during quarter ending June 2026 with growth of 8.30%.
Average Wireless (Mobile) Data Usage per wireless data subscriber per month increased from 26.70 GB during quarter ending March 2026 to 28.39 GB during June 2026 with quarterly rate of growth 6.32%.
Gross Revenue (GR), Applicable Gross Revenue (ApGR) and Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR) of Telecom Service Sector for the quarter ending June 2026 has been ₹1,06,797 Crore, ₹101,036 crore and ₹88,796 Crore respectively.  GR increased by 1.60%, ApGR by 2.43% and AGR increased by 2.40% in the quarter ending June 2025, as compared to previous quarter.
The Y-O-Y rate of growth in GR, ApGR and AGR in the quarter ending June 2026 over the same quarter in last year have been 10.50%, 9.52% and 9.19% respectively.
Pass Through Charges decreased from ₹12,494 Crore in the quarter ending March 2026 to ₹12,241 Crore in the quarter ending June 2026 with quarterly rate of decline of 2.02%. The Y-O-Y rate of growth 17.06% has been recorded in pass-through charges in the quarter ending June 2026.
The License Fee increased from ₹6,936 Crore in the quarter ending March 2026 to ₹7,103 Crore in the quarter ending June 2026. The quarterly and the Y-O-Y rates of growth in license fees are 2.41% and 9.18% respectively in this quarter.
Service-wise composition of Adjusted Gross Revenue
Access services contributed 83.85% of the total Adjusted Gross Revenue of telecom services. In Access services, Gross Revenue (GR), Applicable Gross Revenue (ApGR), Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR), License Fee, Spectrum Usage Charges (SUC) and Pass Through Charges increased by 1.43%, 2.86%, 2.72%, 2.73%, 2.83% and -8.83% respectively in the quarter ending June 2026.
The number of total telephone subscribers in India increased from 1,330.58 million at the end of March 2026 to 1,348.08 million at the end of June 2026, registering a rate of growth 1.31% over the previous quarter. This reflects Year-On-Year (Y-O-Y) rate of growth of 10.65% over the same quarter of last year. The overall Tele-density in India increased from 93.26% in the quarter ending March 2026 to 94.31% in the quarter ending June 2026.
Trends in Telephone subscribers and Tele-density in India
Telephone subscribers in Urban areas increased from 778.79 million at the end of March 2026 to 792.06 million at the end of June 2026 and Urban Tele-density also increased from 151.47% to 153.43% during the same period.
Rural telephone numbers reached 551.79 million at the end of March 2026 to 556.01 million at the end of June 2026 and Rural Tele-density also increased from 60.46% to 60.89% during the same period.
Out of the total subscription, the share of Rural subscription decreased from 41.47% at the end of March 2026 to 41.24% at the end of June 2026.
Composition of Telephone Subscribers
With a net addition of 17.92 million subscribers during the quarter, the total wireless (mobile+FWA) subscriber base increased from 1282.33 million at the end of March 2026 to 1300.25 million at the end of June 2026, registering a rate of growth 1.40% over the previous quarter. On     Y-O-Y basis, wireless subscriptions increased at the rate of 11.05% during the year.
Wireless (mobile + FWA) Tele-density increased from 89.88% at the end of March 2026 to 90.96% at the end of June 2026 with quarterly rate of growth 1.21%.
With a net addition of 16.66 million subscribers during the quarter, the wireless (mobile) subscriber base increased from 1265.73 million at the end of March 2026 to 1282.38 million at the end of June 2026, registering a rate of growth 1.32% over the previous quarter. On Y-O-Y basis, wireless subscriptions also increased at the rate of 10.26% during the year.
Wireless (mobile) Tele-density increased from 88.71% at the end of March 2026 to 89.71% at the end of June 2026 with quarterly rate of growth of 1.13%.

title: BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 Commences Today at National School of Drama in New Delhi
subtitle:
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Graces the Event as the Chief Guest in the presence of Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture

Festival Brings Together Diverse Theatrical Traditions from Nine BRICS Member and Partner Countries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The BRICS Theatre Festival 2026, themed ‘Shared Stories, Shared Futures’, commenced today at the National School of Drama (NSD) in New Delhi. The three-day festival celebrates the diverse theatrical traditions, contemporary performance practices and shared cultural values of BRICS countries. Organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, under India’s BRICS Presidency 2026, the festival will run from 12 to 14 October 2026, bringing together theatre practitioners, scholars, students and cultural representatives from nine BRICS member and partner countries.
Following the successful conclusion of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the festival marks another significant cultural engagement under India’s BRICS Presidency. The participating countries are India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Iran, Vietnam, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia. The festival provides a platform for artistic and cultural exchange through the shared language of theatre.
The opening ceremony was graced by Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Government of India, as the Chief Guest. The ceremony was attended by Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India; Shri Sudhakar Dalela, Secretary (Economic Relations), Ministry of External Affairs, and India’s BRICS Sherpa for 2026; and Shri Chittaranjan Tripathy, Director, National School of Drama. Their Excellencies, Ambassadors and Heads of Mission from the participating countries were also present at the inaugural ceremony.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, said: “We meet today at a moment of considerable consequence for the international community. At a time when nations are increasingly compelled to navigate competing interests, spaces for mutual understanding and constructive dialogue become more precious than ever before.”
“While diplomacy enables nations to negotiate and economic cooperation helps them prosper, culture enables societies to understand one another. It creates connections that transcend political boundaries. Even when our histories, languages and traditions differ, it is this conviction that gives the BRICS Theatre Festival significance beyond the performing arts,” the Union Minister added.
The inaugural day featured the play Samudra Manthan, written by Shri Asif Ali, with design, direction and music by Shri Chittaranjan Tripathy, Director, NSD. The play was staged at the Abhimanch Auditorium on the NSD premises.
The festival’s performances will be staged at venues across New Delhi, including the National School of Drama’s Abhimanch and Sammukh auditoriums, Kamani Auditorium, LTG Auditorium and Meghdoot Theatre. Tickets for the performances will be available through BookMyShow at ₹200 per ticket, offering audiences an opportunity to experience an international showcase of theatre and performance.
The festival features national theatre schools and leading theatre institutions from participating countries. Russia is represented by two theatre groups. India will present two theatre productions, while the participating countries will showcase works reflecting their diverse languages, cultural perspectives, theatrical traditions and contemporary creative expressions. The curated programme spans a wide spectrum of theatrical forms, including classical, contemporary and experimental theatre.
India has assumed the BRICS Presidency for 2026 under the theme ‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability’, with a people-centric approach to strengthening cooperation among BRICS nations. Under this Presidency, the BRICS Culture Track prioritises collaboration in cultural and creative industries, the protection of cultural heritage, and the role of culture in climate resilience and sustainable development. The Theatre Festival complements these priorities by fostering artistic exchange, cultural dialogue and people-to-people connections through live performance.
To encourage artistic engagement and professional exchange, interactive workshops and discussion sessions will be organised on the mornings following performances, involving directors, cast members and crew. Covering artistic vision, performance traditions, acting methodologies and stagecraft, these sessions will feature discussions, audience interaction and collaborative exercises to promote intercultural learning, knowledge-sharing and long-term collaboration. Through diverse stories and performance traditions, the festival seeks to celebrate distinct cultural identities while strengthening mutual understanding and cooperation among BRICS nations.
The National School of Drama (NSD), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, serves as the nodal agency for organising the BRICS Theatre Festival 2026. By bringing together theatre institutions and practitioners from participating countries, NSD supports the festival’s objective of encouraging artistic exchange and strengthening international cultural engagement.
The BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 serves not only as a showcase of theatrical excellence but also as a platform for cultural dialogue, professional exchange and people-to-people engagement, aligned with the broader objectives of BRICS cooperation. Through theatre, the festival brings together stories, artists and audiences across borders, strengthening cultural understanding and creating opportunities for continued collaboration.

, while highlighting the contribution of Indian defence industries and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) towards strengthening indigenous naval capabilities.
Designed for operations in coastal and shallow waters, INS Mangrol is equipped to undertake
Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), underwater surveillance and Low-Intensity Maritime Operations (LIMO), along with mine warfare-related tasks.
Its advanced sensors, sonar and weapon systems enhance its capability to detect, track and counter underwater threats in the challenging littoral environment. Powered by three diesel engine-driven waterjet propulsion units, the ship offers high manoeuvrability and rapid response, essential for operations in shallow and confined waters.
VAdm Sanjay Vatsayan, in his address, congratulated the Indian Navy and CSL on the commissioning of INS Mangrol. He highlighted the importance of indigenous warships in strengthening India's maritime surveillance and anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in the evolving maritime security environment. He also emphasised the growing capabilities of India's indigenous shipbuilding industry and the Indian Navy's continued commitment to technological advancement, operational preparedness and self-reliance in defence manufacturing.
INS Mangrol derives its name from the coastal town and prominent fishing harbour of Mangrol in Junagadh district of Gujarat.
The ship also carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until April 2004, continuing the naval tradition of preserving the names of distinguished warships.
The commissioning of INS Mangrol marks another significant milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities and coastal defence preparedness. The ship will contribute to safeguarding India's coastal approaches and maritime interests, enhancing maritime domain awareness and countering underwater threats. Its induction further reinforces the Indian Navy's commitment to maritime security, regional stability and self-reliance in warship construction, in furtherance of India's maritime interests in the
Indian Ocean Region.

title: EXERCISE TARANG SHAKTI 2026: POWER IN PARTNERSHIP,  STRENGTH IN SELF-RELIANCE
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti, hosted by the Indian Air Force at Air Force Station Jodhpur from 26 September to 12 October 2026, marks a significant milestone in India’s growing engagement with partner air forces and its emergence as a key contributor to regional and global security. With the theme ‘Power in Partnership’, the multinational air exercise brings together seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs)—Australia, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America—along with 32 observer nations. The participation reflects the growing international interest in India’s operational capabilities, professional standards and expanding aerospace and defence ecosystem.
Building on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024, Tarang Shakti 2026 provided a platform for complex joint missions, exchange of operational experience and enhanced interoperability among participating air forces. The exercise brought together diverse combat, transport, surveillance and air-to-air refuelling capabilities, enabling aircrew, mission planners and support personnel to gain valuable insights into each other’s operational philosophies and procedures. The presence of a large number of observer nations further expanded the exercise’s strategic significance, reinforcing India’s commitment to constructive defence engagement and international cooperation.
The contemporary relevance of the exercise is underscored by the decisive role of air power in Operation Sindoor, which demonstrated the Indian Air Force’s ability to execute precise, calibrated and effective operations in furtherance of national security objectives. The operation highlighted the importance of operational preparedness, integrated planning, credible deterrence and the effective application of air power in a complex security environment. The experience gained from operational employment reinforces the value of multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti in advancing professional understanding and preparing for the evolving challenges of modern warfare.
Atmanirbharta in defence remains central to India’s vision of a technologically advanced and self-reliant nation. The participation of indigenous platforms, including the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, underscores the progress made in developing advanced aerospace capabilities through indigenous design, engineering and manufacturing. Their presence alongside international platforms reflects India’s growing ability to develop and field modern military systems. Tarang Shakti also provides an opportunity for partner nations to appreciate the capabilities of India’s aerospace and defence industry, in keeping with the Government of India’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the growing role of Indian industry in defence innovation and manufacturing.
The canvas of Tarang Shakti extends well beyond flying operations. Industrial tours expose participating contingents to India’s expanding aerospace, defence manufacturing and technological ecosystem, while professional engagements promote the exchange of knowledge and experience. Yoga sessions, heritage visits and other interactions provide opportunities for participants to experience India’s traditions and cultural ethos. The International Night serves as a celebration of the diverse cultures and traditions represented by participating nations, strengthening camaraderie and mutual understanding beyond the operational environment.
Public outreach has been another important dimension of the exercise. The Open Day drew more than 20,000 visitors, offering the public an opportunity to witness the might of the Indian Air Force and gain a closer appreciation of its aircraft, operational capabilities and personnel. Such engagement strengthens the bond between the Armed Forces and citizens, while inspiring younger generations to learn about aviation, national security and service to the nation.
The exercise also acquires added significance as India celebrates the 94th Anniversary of the Indian Air Force. Over more than nine decades, the IAF has evolved from a modest force into a modern, multi-dimensional aerospace power, with expanding operational reach, advanced platforms, integrated capabilities and an increasingly strong indigenous technological base. Its operational experience, professional excellence and continuing modernisation reflect an institution committed to meeting emerging challenges while remaining prepared for the demands of future warfare.
Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 exemplifies this journey of transformation. By combining operational capability, indigenous innovation, international engagement and public outreach, the exercise reinforces India’s commitment to national security, defence self-reliance and enduring partnerships. As the Indian Air Force marks its 94th Anniversary, ‘Power in Partnership’ captures a defining principle of its outlook: a strong, capable and self-reliant air force, working with trusted partners to contribute to peace, stability and security.

title: CAPSS-IAF CONDUCT SEMINAR AS PART OF  EXERCISE TARANG SHAKTI - 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Centre for Aerospace Power and Strategic Studies (CAPSS), together with the Indian Air Force (IAF), organised a seminar on 09 October 2026 at the Air Force Auditorium, Subroto Park in New Delhi, on the side-lines of Exercise Tarang        Shakti-26. The seminar, on the theme “The Central Role of Air Power in the Evolving Battlespace," brought together representatives of partner Air Forces from all continents, senior military leaders, academia industry and the media to examine how air power is adapting to the changing character of warfare.
Fresh from the operational experiences gained during this flying exercise, the teams now carried forward their engagement to the conceptual level during the seminar. The seminar sought to identify doctrinal priorities and areas for future cooperation and encouraged informed dialogue among partner Air Forces.
Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd.), Director General, CAPSS, delivered the welcome address. He elucidated the role of air power in contemporary conflicts and highlighted the contribution of CAPSS in fostering it. CAPSS was established in 2001 as an autonomous research and analysis body focused on national security, nuclear, and aerospace issues. The year 2026 marks the Silver Jubilee of CAPSS.
Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff, delivered the inaugural address. The CAS underscored the need for integrated capabilities, operational resilience and enhanced interoperability to meet emerging challenges in air warfare. He stressed the concurrent development of manned and unmanned operations, guided by clear employment doctrines, and the integration of all sensors, weapon systems and unmanned platforms with communication and data networks from the outset. He also called for strengthening supply chains, adopting innovative training methods and enhancing capacity to sustain prolonged operations. Highlighting air power’s role in humanitarian assistance, support to partner countries and advancing the nation’s international standing, he emphasized focused deliberations on information warfare and perception management, along with greater exchange of operational experience and enhanced cooperation among air forces to address common challenges.
The first working session looked at the transformation of air warfare in the 21st  century and was chaired by Air Chief Marshal VR Chaudhari, former Chief of the Air Staff. The session explored the shift from air superiority to battlespace control, decision dominance and the role of media as a strategic weapon. The panellists argued that air power is no longer about owning the skies alone; it involves an entire operational ecosystem. The session engaged both traditional concepts as well as modern themes. The second session was chaired by Air Marshal Stephen Chappell, Chief of the Air Staff, Royal Australian Air Force. The session examined air power as a strategy of national power, covering deterrence, coercion, escalation control, and human capital development. This session debated the necessary reforms in air power to meet emergent and future requirements of the battlefield holistically. It also dissected the role of air power in deterrence and escalation control.
The discussion were insightful and engaging, offering participants and online viewers  valuable, rich and diverse perspectives on the future of air power.

title: Indian Army launches ‘Bharat Rice’ for troops in the presence of Raksha Mantri and Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
subtitle:
This superior quality rice to be delivered directly to Army Supply Depots, including in Ladakh & North East

MoU inked with FCI to enable use of its warehousing, manpower & material-handling resources during operational contingencies

The initiative embodies a collective resolve where the hard work of a farmer transforms into the strength of a soldier, says Shri Rajnath Singh

“Resilient supply chains and soldiers’ welfare integral to national security”

“Op Sindoor highlighted the need for resilient logistics chains to sustain military operations”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 1:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Army launched ‘Bharat Rice’ for the defence forces, at a ceremony graced by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Shri Pralhad Joshi in New Delhi on October 12, 2026. The event also featured the signing of an MoU between the Indian Army and Food Corporation of India (FCI) for utilisation of its infrastructure during operational contingencies. This superior quality rice will be delivered directly to Army Supply Depots, including those in far-flung areas of Ladakh and the North East, instead of being collected by Army depots from local FCI facilities.
In his address, Raksha Mantri described ‘Bharat Rice’ as a bond of trust that begins in the farmer’s field and extends to the soldier’s plate. He stated that the initiative provides a tangible form to the spirit of ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ as it embodies a collective resolve where the hard work of a farmer transforms into the strength of a soldier. “This superior-quality rice will be provided in accordance with standard specifications. Furthermore, we are ensuring ergonomic packaging. While this initiative might appear small, it offers immense operational relief to the soldiers responsible for transporting rations to remote and difficult terrains,” he added.
Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that the soldiers’ operational readiness is not defined by weaponry alone; it also lies in their physical health, mental balance, morale and stamina, especially as they serve in harshest of conditions. He termed the welfare of soldiers as not a peripheral issue, but an integral component of national security, adding that healthy food, robust equipment and complete training boost the morale of troops, making them ready to face every challenge, and protect the nation.
Raksha Mantri asserted that in modern-day warfare, weapons, platforms, and technology are not the only critical elements; logistics itself is combat power. He stated that wars today are not won solely on the front lines, and factors such as the strength of supply chains, storage capacity, transportation networks, warehousing infrastructure, and the ability for timely replenishment play an equally crucial role.
“The strategic analysis of Operation Sindoor indicated that warning times could be extremely short in future conflicts. Scenarios involving zero-warning situations and the integration of technology into warfare could severely test our preparedness. Such conflicts could also put the endurance of our logistics chains and supply networks to the test. Therefore, we must build logistics resilience to sustain our operations. This MoU with FCI represents a significant step in that direction,” said Shri Rajnath Singh.
Raksha Mantri added that FCI possesses warehouses, storage infrastructure, modern silos, material handling equipment, and trained manpower across the country, including the operationally significant areas. This initiative is proof that the country's existing national capacity can be aligned with national security requirements when the need arises, he said, adding that it represents a dual-use approach, wherein the country's infrastructure and capabilities serve not just a single purpose, but cater to both civil and military needs.
Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that just as fighter aircraft are now landing on expressways, and roads & bridges built by Border Roads Organisation are being utilised by local residents too, FCI godowns will no longer be limited to food storage; they will become an integral part of the Indian Army’s supply chain. “This approach will optimise resources and strengthen national resilience. Integrating existing infrastructure with operational planning allows us to save time and utilise resources more effectively. This MoU is far more than a mere administrative arrangement. It acts as a force multiplier for operational preparedness and reflects our ‘Whole-of-Government’ and ‘Whole-of-Nation’ approach,” he said.
Raksha Mantri highlighted the Government’s focus on every aspect of our soldiers' welfare, adding that emphasis has been placed on self-reliance and modernisation across all sectors, from weaponry and technology to clothing, equipment, and training. “Today, India produces a significant portion of its defence requirements domestically,” he said, underlining that innovation and coordination are the basis of the Government’s resolve to continuously provide best quality products to the soldiers, make the supply chains more resilient, ensure timely deliveries to forward areas, and better utilise civilian infrastructure for national security. He added that when the soldiers stand guard at the borders, they must have the confidence that the entire country stands with them. He termed boosting the morale of soldiers as the Government’s priority, emphasising that this resolve is not of the government alone; it is shared by the farmers, the cooperative sector, the civil administration, and the nation at large.
Speaking on the occasion, Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Shri Pralhad Joshi appreciated the ‘Bharat Rice’ initiative, and said that it is a matter of pride for his department to provide superior quality rice to those who protect the nation with unmatched bravery and dedication. “To provide quality food to the nation’s protectors and cater to their needs is our duty,” he said.
Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Secretary (Food and Public Distribution) Shri Sanjeev Chopra and senior officials from the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, FCI, National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Limited (NAFED) and the cooperative sector were present on the occasion.
About Bharat Rice
Spearheaded by the Directorate General of Supplies and Transport, the Bharat Rice initiative is based on sustained feedback from troops and is aimed at improving the quality of rations. The rice will be milled to prescribed defence specifications and supplied through NAFED during Financial Year 2026-27. It will undergo requisite quality-control checks and will be free from foreign matter and admixtures, with minimal broken, damaged and discoloured grains.
Procurement in 10 kg and 30 kg bags will further ease handling and transportation, particularly at forward posts. The initiative follows nearly 18 months of coordination among the Army, FCI, NAFED and the Department of Food & Public Distribution.
The MoU with FCI draws upon operational lessons, including those from Operation Sindoor, which highlighted the requirement for resilient logistics arrangements during contingencies that may arise at short notice and extend over prolonged periods. It provides the Indian Army a formal framework to utilise identified FCI warehousing infrastructure, labour resources and material-handling equipment during operational contingencies.
Coordination will be undertaken at formation level between the Army’s Supply and Transport elements and FCI’s Regional and Divisional Offices and integrated into operational logistics plans. The MoU will remain valid for five years, extendable by mutual consent.
The arrangement will enable additional storage, rapid mobilisation, dispersion and forward positioning of rations, stores and equipment closer to operational areas, thereby strengthening the responsiveness and resilience of military logistics while optimising existing national infrastructure. The initiative reflects a whole-of-government approach aligned with the vision of PM Gati Shakti.
The Indian Army has also undertaken a series of measures in recent years to improve ration quality and scales, including additional rations for Agniveer recruits and greater commonality in ration scales across the three Services. Organic rations are also proposed to be introduced.
