title: Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates and Lays Foundation Stones for Development Projects of ₹331 Crore in Mizoram
subtitle:
Union Minister Dedicates Five Projects Worth ₹102 Crore and Lays Foundation Stones for Five Projects of ₹228.54 Crore, Strengthening Connectivity, Power, Water Supply, Healthcare, Education, Sports and Culture

Northeast Is Emerging as an Engine of India's Growth; Development Must Preserve Mizoram's Unique Identity and Natural Heritage

Mizoram Records Over 5 Lakh Tourist Visits in First Half of 2026: Scindia

Union Minister Scindia Announces ₹6,812.30 Crore investment by MDoNER for Northeast in FY 2026–27
ministry: Ministry of Development of North-East Region
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, today inaugurated development projects and laid foundation stones of new initiatives worth ₹331 crore, in Mizoram.Shri Scindia is on  two-day visit of Mizoram.
Upon his arrival in Aizwal, the Union Minister proceeded to Tuivamit and  inaugurated five project worth ₹102 Crore. Union Minister also laid foundation stone of five projects of ₹228.54 crore. Projects cover critical sectors including road connectivity, power transmission, water supply, healthcare, education, sports and cultural infrastructure.
Addressing the gathering in the presence of Mizoram Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma and other dignitaries, Union Minister Scindia said that the development initiatives reflected the Government of India's commitment to transforming connectivity into economic opportunities and improving the quality of life across Mizoram.
Describing Mizoram as a land of majestic mountains and even greater aspirations, the Union Minister said, "Geography may shape the landscape. It must never shape the limits of the  people."
He emphasised that the occasion was not merely about inaugurating infrastructure or laying foundation stones, but about creating opportunities for farmers, entrepreneurs, young people and communities across the state.
Northeast Emerging as an Engine of India's Growth---
Highlighting the growing economic significance of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said that while India is recording economic growth of around 7–7.5%, the Northeast is increasingly emerging as a major contributor to the country's growth trajectory.
He observed that it would not be an exaggeration to describe the North Eastern Region as an engine driving India's development forward.
The Union Minister noted that this was his 35th visit to the North Eastern Region and said that every visit strengthened his commitment to the development of the eight Ashtalakshmi states.
"Every time I come here, I go back recharged and with a renewed commitment towards the Ashtalakshmi states," he said.
Referring to his longstanding association with Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma, Shri Scindia fondly recalled the close relationship between the Chief Minister and his late father. In a lighter moment, he remarked that he represented the second generation of that relationship and appreciated the Chief Minister's youthful energy and enthusiasm.
Shri Scindia also highlighted the region's extraordinary natural beauty and ecological wealth, stressing that development must proceed alongside environmental conservation.
Connectivity Transforming Mizoram's Development Landscape ---
The Union Minister highlighted the significant improvements in Mizoram's connectivity through roads, railways and air transport, observing that the state was becoming increasingly connected not only through infrastructure but also through stronger bonds between people.
He described the 51.38-kilometre Bairabi–Sairang railway line as a historic milestone that brought Mizoram onto India's railway map and transformed access to major economic centers.
The railway connectivity has facilitated the movement of more than 15 lakh passengers through over 1,100 train trips, linking Aizawl with Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The introduction of the Sairang–Silchar service has further strengthened connectivity with the Barak Valley.
Highlighting another landmark achievement, Shri Scindia referred to the arrival of the first Food Corporation of India food-grain rake at Sairang in March 2026, carrying approximately 26,000 quintals of rice from Punjab in 42 wagons.
He said that the direct movement of food grains from Punjab to Mizoram by rail would have been difficult to imagine a decade ago and demonstrated how improved connectivity was bringing distant regions of the country closer together.
Referring to tourism, Shri Scindia noted that Mizoram had recorded 4,94,362 domestic tourist visits and 7,389 foreign tourist visits during the first six months of 2026, reflecting the state's growing appeal as a tourism destination.
Mizoram Ginger Mission to Strengthen Farmers' Livelihoods --
Highlighting the state's agricultural potential, Shri Scindia described Mizo ginger as a unique strength and economic identity of Mizoram.
He said that the ₹189.79 crore Mizoram Ginger Mission would bring nearly 20,000 farming households into an integrated value chain encompassing cultivation, processing, branding, connectivity and access to national and international markets.
The Union Minister emphasised that the objective was not merely to increase ginger production but to ensure that farmers and local communities received a greater share of the economic value generated.
"Mizo ginger is Mizoram's USP; our mission is to make sure the value stays where the ginger grows," he said.
₹331 Crore Development Push Across Key Sectors -
Detailing the Ministry of DoNER's continued investments in the state, Shri Scindia informed the gathering that the Ministry has been allocated ₹6,812.30 crore for the North Eastern Region in the current financial year.
He stated that 375 projects worth ₹4,617.70 crore have been taken up in Mizoram, of which 295 projects, involving an investment of ₹2,692.31 crore, have already been completed.
Congratulating the Government of Mizoram for its cooperation and efforts in implementing development projects, the Union Minister said that the completion of nearly four out of every five projects demonstrated the progress achieved through coordinated efforts between the Centre and the State.
The Union Minister highlighted ten development projects worth approximately ₹331 crore, comprising five projects worth around ₹102 crore dedicated to the people and five projects worth ₹228.54 crore for which foundation stones were laid.
He described these initiatives as investments in both
"Routes and Roots"
— routes representing the physical infrastructure required to connect people and markets, and roots representing institutions that nurture health, education, culture and talent.
"Routes take Mizoram to the world. Roots keep Mizoram Mizo," he said.
Five Development Projects Worth ₹102 Crore Dedicated to the People
The projects inaugurated and dedicated to the people include:
Daido–Vangkawt Road, Champhai (₹17.24 crore):
A 3.33-kilometre road developed under NESIDS-Roads to improve connectivity in the Mizo Ginger pilot region and facilitate the movement of agricultural produce to markets.
132 kV Bairabi–West Phaileng Transmission Line via Mamit (₹54.95 crore):
A 74-circuit-kilometre power transmission line aimed at strengthening the state's electricity transmission network and improving power infrastructure.
Augmentation of North Vanlaiphai Water Supply Scheme (₹20.50 crore):
A project designed to improve access to water supply and strengthen essential public infrastructure.
AYUSH Development Centre (₹2.64 crore):
An initiative to strengthen institutional capacity and healthcare infrastructure in the AYUSH sector.
Aizawl Institute of Arts & Music for the North Eastern Region, Tuivamit Tlang (₹6.90 crore):
Developed under the Schemes of the North Eastern Council, the institute aims to promote artistic talent, preserve cultural traditions and create professional opportunities in music and the arts.
Speaking about the Aizawl Institute of Arts & Music, Shri Scindia praised the exceptional musical talent of Mizoram and expressed his admiration for the musicians who performed during the programme.
He appreciated the energy, enthusiasm and skill displayed by the performers, particularly the drummers, and said that their performances reflected the artistic excellence and vibrant cultural spirit of Mizoram.
Foundation Stones Laid for Five Projects Worth ₹228.54 Crore --
The Union Minister also laid foundation stones for five development projects aimed at expanding connectivity and strengthening social infrastructure across the state.
These include:
Pukzing–Silsuri Road, Mamit (₹100.24 crore):
A 21-kilometre road project under NESIDS-Roads aimed at improving all-weather connectivity. Shri Scindia highlighted that Silsuri is among the villages identified for a new bank branch, where inadequate road connectivity has remained a constraint.
Tualpui–Champhai Road (₹57.01 crore):
A 21-kilometre road project covering Khawzawl and Champhai districts to strengthen regional connectivity and improve access to markets and essential services.
Oil Palm Link Road (₹26.49 crore):
A 32.70-kilometre road project under NESIDS-Roads connecting areas across Kolasib, Mamit, Lunglei and Lawngtlai, expected to benefit nearly 60,000 people across 19 villages by improving agricultural transportation and access to essential services.
40-Bed Hostel for ANM School, Zemabawk, Aizawl (₹10 crore):
A project under NESIDS-OTRI aimed at strengthening nursing education and supporting the training of healthcare professionals.
Sports Infrastructure Development in Mizoram (₹34.80 crore):
An initiative to create improved sporting facilities and opportunities for young athletes, building on Mizoram's strong sporting culture and contributions to Indian football and other disciplines.
Development Must Reflect the Spirit of Hnatlang
Concluding his address, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia invoked Mizoram's traditional spirit of Hnatlang, a community practice in which people voluntarily come together to undertake collective work for the welfare of their village and neighbours.
He described the development initiatives as an expression of Hnatlang on a larger scale, bringing together the Central Government, the State Government and the people in a shared mission of progress.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) dedicates
Cyclone Warning and Marine Weather Services Decision Support System (DSS), an interactive WebGIS-based platform, to the nation on 12th October 2026
. The launch took place during the bi-annual Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting for the post-monsoon season (October-December), 2026 under the chairmanship of Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of Meteorology, IMD and 3rd Vice President of World Meteorological Organisation. The above DSS platform for public is available on IMD website (
www.mausam.imd.gov.in
) and Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) website (
www.rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in
). The url of the above web-based platform is given below:
https://dss.imd.gov.in/dwr_img/GIS/marine.php
DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith cone of uncertainty and district-wise rainfall warning
The
DSS is a user-friendly, interactive platform
that brings critical cyclone and marine weather information together in one place, making it easier for users, including disaster management authorities, government agencies and the general public, to understand potential hazards and their likely impacts. Through interactive maps and visualisations of cyclone tracks, intensity, winds, rainfall, storm surge and rainfall forecasts for river catchments, the platform helps users access relevant information and make informed decisions. It aims to bridge the gap between weather forecasts and their practical use, enabling better preparedness, timely action and enhanced public safety during cyclones and other severe weather events.
DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith wind distribution and district-wise rainfall warning
DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith wind distribution and storm surge warning
The occasion holds special significance as IMD successfully predicted
Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Phailin (2013) and Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Hudhud (2014)
(both incidentally crossed coast on 12th October, 2013 and 2014 respectively) and marked important milestones in India’s disaster preparedness, earning international recognition for the country’s early-warning capabilities.
IMD has been conducting this meeting bi-annually since 2008.
The exercise serves as a vital platform for reviewing preparedness for the ensuing cyclone season, assessing progress on previous action points, sharing IMD’s latest initiatives and addressing operational challenges.
It also fosters close liaison and coordination among IMD, disaster management authorities, defence forces, state governments and other user agencies, ensuring that forecasts and warnings are effectively utilised for timely action on the ground.
The meeting witnessed participation from more than 30 organisations across the country, with approximately 230 participants, including 180 joining online and 50 attending in person
. The participating organisations included the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Indian Navy (IN), Indian Air Force (IAF), Indian Coast Guard (ICG), Central Water Commission (CWC), Press Information Bureau (PIB), state disaster management authorities and fisheries departments. Scientific and technical organisations included the India Meteorological Department (IMD), National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT). Representatives from coastal states and Union Territories, including West Bengal, Odisha, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Lakshadweep, Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Puducherry also participated. Delegates from various ministries and departments, including the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Ministry of Heavy Industries, Department of Consumer Affairs, Directorate General of Light House & Light Ships (DGLL), and other sectoral stakeholders, attended the meeting. The participation provided an important platform for strengthening inter-agency coordination, sharing operational requirements and enhancing preparedness for the upcoming cyclone season.
The meeting commenced with a
presentation on the activities and recent advancements of the IMD in the field of cyclone warning and marine weather services, followed by a review of the Action Taken Report
on the recommendations of the Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting held in April.
A live demonstration of the newly launched, user-oriented Decision Support System (DSS)
showcased its interactive features and capabilities to provide location-specific information on cyclones and associated hazards. The demonstration was followed by valuable comments, suggestions and feedback from participating stakeholders, aimed at further improving the platform and enhancing its operational utility.
The meeting reaffirmed IMD’s commitment to strengthening early-warning services
, enhancing inter-agency coordination and translating accurate forecasts into timely action to minimise loss of life and property during cyclones.
A total of 230 Disaster Managers and stakeholders participated in the meeting

title: APARC General Assembly 2026 Begins at IITM Pune: Global Experts Gather to Shape the Future of Atmospheric and Climate Science
date:

content:
The inaugural function of the Atmospheric Processes and their Role in Climate (APARC) General Assembly 2026 took place today at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune by the Chief Guest, Dr Srinivasa Kumar Tummala (Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India) (virtually), Guest of Honor, Ms. Ko Barrett (Deputy Secretary-General of the UN WMO) (virtually), Dr. Hinduma
thi Palanisamy (Scientific Officer, WCRP, WMO), Dr Stephanie Evan (CNRS Research Scientist at The Laboratory of the Atmosphere and Cyclones (Laboratoire de l'Atmosphère et des Cyclones- LACy), Réunion Island, France & APARC Co-chair), Dr. Hella Garny (DLR Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Germany, & APARC LOC International), Dr Suryachandra Rao (Director, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology), and Dr Suvarna Fadnavis (Chair, Scientific Organizing Committee & Project Director CCCR, IITM).
Marking a historic moment, India is taking the lead in hosting this landmark quadrennial event, bringing together world-renowned scientists, researchers, students, and policymakers to discuss breakthrough scientific advances and foster collaborative initiatives in climate and atmospheric sciences.
The five-day assembly (October 12–16, 2026) convenes over 550 participants from across Europe, the Americas, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia, and beyond. This includes 380 in-person attendees—250 national and 130 international delegates—along with approximately 180 global researchers joining virtually.
Strong Leadership and Keynote Address
The event commenced with an opening keynote address delivered by
Dr. Suryachandra A. Rao
, Director of IITM, Pune, titled:
"Modeling the Monsoon: Avenues for bridging the gap between potential predictability and prediction skill."
Key dignitaries and atmospheric scientists leading the assembly include, Dr. Stephanie Evan, CNRS Scientist, France (APARC Co-Chair), Dr. Olaf Morgenstern, Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), Germany (APARC Co-Chair), Dr. Hindhumati Palanisamy, World Meteorological Organization (WMO), Geneva, Prof. Paul Kushner, University of Toronto, Canada, Dr. Suryachandra A. Rao, Director, IITM, Pune and Dr. Suvarna Fadnavis, Project Director, Centre for Climate Change Research, IITM
Addressing Critical Themes for Societal Benefit
APARC is a core project of the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP). Held once every four years, the General Assembly serves as a global platform to identify emerging research gaps, strengthen scientific partnerships, and develop actionable roadmaps to address pressing climate challenges for societal benefit.
The discussions and connections established during the meeting are expected to contribute to future APARC activities and help shape new directions in atmospheric and climate research.
This General Assembly’s scientific programme features
67 oral presentations
(including 9 keynotes, 17 invited talks, and 41 contributed talks) alongside
more than 400 poster presentations
. The assembly is structured around six core themes:
High-resolution representation of the climate system
Atmospheric composition and its variability in a changing climate
Dynamical and thermodynamic fingerprints of climate forcing
Circulation, composition, and extreme events in the tropics
Climate prediction from subseasonal to decadal timescales
APARC science with and for society
Special focus is placed on emerging frontiers, including artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) in climate modeling, atmospheric chemistry, extreme event forecasting, and connecting fundamental climate research with actionable societal applications.
Empowering the Next Generation of Scientists
With over 120 students and 150 Early Career Researchers (ECRs) attending, the conference strongly emphasizes mentorship and networking. The poster sessions and collaborative forums offer early-career scientists’ direct interaction with international leaders, fostering new ideas and global research partnerships that will help guide the future trajectory of atmospheric research.
About APARC & WCRP
Atmospheric Processes and their Role in Climate (APARC) is a core project of the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP). It focuses on understanding atmospheric drivers and processes that control weather patterns and global climate dynamics.

title: CAQM reviews Zone-wise Preparedness of all 12 MCD Zones for Road Dust Mitigation and Deep Cleaning of Roads in Delhi
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of its continued efforts to strengthen dust mitigation measures and improve road cleanliness for effective air pollution control in Delhi, the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the chairmanship of Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, CAQM, today held a hearing to review the actions taken and preparedness of all 12 zones of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). The review focused on the removal of accumulated and legacy dust, garbage and Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste from roads, roadsides, medians, footpaths and other open areas.
The Hearing was held pursuant to the Commission’s notice dated 7th October 2026, issued following an inspection conducted on 3rd October 2026, during which instances of high visible road dust and accumulation of C&D waste were observed on road stretches maintained by the Public Works Department (PWD) and cleaned by MCD, indicating the need for further strengthening of dust mitigation and cleaning measures on the ground. The Commissioner, MCD and concerned Deputy Commissioners (DCs) of the 12 zones of MCD were called upon to explain the actions taken and preparedness for addressing the identified gaps. During the hearing, the Deputy Commissioners, MCD made zone-wise presentations detailing the cleaning and sweeping operations undertaken, dust mitigation measures implemented, enforcement actions taken and preparedness for further improving road cleanliness and abating road dust emissions.
The presentations highlighted sustained efforts towards mechanized road sweeping, water sprinkling, road washing and intensive deep cleaning of major roads and identified air pollution hotspots. Measures for the removal and scientific disposal of accumulated legacy dust, silt, malba, garbage and C&D waste were also presented, along with cleaning of footpaths, road edges, medians, kerb stones and other areas prone to dust accumulation. The deployment of mechanical road sweeping machines (MRSMs), water sprinklers, water tankers, anti-smog guns, jetting machines and dedicated sanitation teams form part of the ongoing dust suppression and cleaning operations by the 12 zones of MCD in Delhi.
The zones also presented measures for repairing potholes and damaged road stretches, paving unpaved areas, greening dust-prone patches and improving sanitation at vulnerable locations. Preparedness for the winter season includes special deep-cleaning drives, hotspot-specific interventions, improved management of designated C&D waste collection points, regular field inspections and enforcement against open burning, improper waste disposal and other polluting activities. The need for coordinated action(s) with PWD, DDA, DJB, Railways and other concerned agencies to address dust-generating activities and resolve pending infrastructure-related issues was also highlighted.
The review covered the Outer North Zone (Narela), City SP Zone (Old Delhi), Civil Line Zone (North), Rohini Zone (North West), Central North Zone (Keshavpuram), Central Zone (Karol Bagh), South Zone, Central Zone (South East), Najafgarh Zone (South West), West Zone, Shahdara South Zone (East) and Shahdara North Zone (North East).
The Commission emphasized the need for effective implementation of the measures presented to ensure improved road cleanliness and sustained reduction in road dust emissions. Further, continued gaps in the implementation of prescribed dust mitigation measures would be viewed seriously and that appropriate action(s) including prosecution, may be initiated against the responsible agencies or officials for non-compliance.
The Deputy Commissioners, MCD were directed to ensure effective utilization of deployed machinery and sanitation manpower thus augmenting the machinery as per the quantum of work to be done and actual requirement. Further, regular cleaning of identified road stretches, prompt removal and scientific disposal of accumulated dust and C&D waste and priority attention to damaged roads and other dust-generating locations, should be focused. Close field-level supervision, regular monitoring of progress and accountability for gaps in implementation were also reviewed.
The Commission noted the actions taken by MCD and reiterated that the removal of accumulated dust and garbage from roads and open areas must be ensured within the stipulated timeline of 31st October 2026. All concerned zones and agencies were directed to ensure strict compliance with the Commission’s Statutory Directions and strengthen dust mitigation measures for effective control and mitigation of road dust pollution and improvement of air quality in Delhi-NCR.

He highlighted India’s progress in wildlife conservation, increase in forest and tree cover, carbon sequestration, woodland/wetland conservation, and landscape restoration through citizen-engaging initiatives such as Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam, besides MISHTI, Aravalli Green Wall and Nagar Van Yojana. The Minister emphasised that the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’ must integrate economic development with ecological security. He identified human-wildlife conflict, forest fires, climate change and balancing development with conservation as major challenges requiring scientific approaches and community participation.
The Minister stated that India is lucky to have wide diversity of climate, ecosystems and biodiversity. He said that an IFS officer needs to adapt and efficiently take a leadership role at the ground level in forest and wildlife conservation. Bioresources are the most important and vital resources on this planet, hence the officers are being given cross-cutting Ministry level policy making exposure besides the field level implementation experience, he informed. The Minister encouraged the officers to think out of the box and find practical solutions to the challenges in their field.
Highlighting the evolving role of the Indian Forest Service, Shri Yadav urged officers to move beyond traditional regulatory functions and become leaders, innovators and facilitators of sustainable development. He stressed the importance of emerging technologies, including GIS, remote sensing and artificial intelligence, alongside continuous capacity building and community engagement by utilising traditional knowledge. The Minister called upon officers to strengthen institutions, adopt innovative approaches for efficient decision making and preparing forest management plans, and uphold their responsibility towards safeguarding India’s ecological future.

The 68 participants from 18 cadres bring diverse field and policy experience, with professional interests spanning wildlife conservation governance, climate-resilient forestry, habitat restoration, landscape restoration and environmental policy implementation.

Line Ministry Module
would provide the officers exposure to key Central Ministries and organisations to enhance understanding of inter-sectoral linkages and policy frameworks.
Thematic visits
to Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh would focus on best practices in wildlife management, biodiversity conservation, ecotourism and community-based forest management.
The
Management Module
would be structured around leadership and decision-making, human resource and financial management, governance of forest commons, negotiation and conflict resolution, change management, communication and ethical leadership. Finally, the
Forestry Module
would address emerging issues including environmental conventions, AI in forestry, digital transformation, national wildlife leadership, biodiversity governance, climate finance, FRA issues, watershed management, recent FCA amendments and human-wildlife conflict.

title: Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Visits Madurai Ornamental Fisheries Cluster and Interacts with Progressive Ornamental Fish Farmers
subtitle: Union Secretary Emphasises Quality Broodstock, Scientific Breeding, Biosecurity and Market Linkages to Boost Ornamental Fisheries
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, visited Padimuneeswarar Integrated Ornamental Fish Farm at Village Mukkampatti, Melur, Madurai District, Tamil Nadu, on
12 October 2026
. Madurai in Tamil Nadu has been notified as an Ornamental Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY by Government of India.
The visit aimed to assess the progress and potential of ornamental fisheries, interact with fish farmers and entrepreneurs, and further strengthen the development of the ornamental fisheries cluster.
During the interaction, the Union Secretary discussed ornamental fish varieties, broodstock and seed availability, water quality, aquatic animal health, transportation and marketing with fish farmers and entrepreneurs. He encouraged scientific breeding and rearing practices, promotion of high-value indigenous species, and collective efforts to enhance access to technology, institutional finance and markets.
Emphasising the Government’s cluster-based development approach, the Secretary stated that 34 notified fisheries clusters are being developed across the country  through coordinated interventions covering production, input supply, infrastructure, capacity building, processing, value addition, branding, logistics and market linkages. This approach aims to address value-chain gaps, enhance competitiveness and improve farmers’ incomes.
Padimuneeswarar Integrated Ornamental Fish Farm was established under PMMSY at a project cost of ₹25 lakh. The farm breeds and rears more than 30 varieties of ornamental fish, including guppy, platy, molly, swordtail, goldfish, koi carp, cichlids and fighter fish. With four production cycles annually, the unit produces approximately 2 lakh ornamental fish seeds per year and generates an estimated annual income of ₹3.75 lakh. The farm supplies ornamental fish to domestic markets in Tamil Nadu and Keralam.
Background
India’s fisheries sector has made significant progress, with fish production reaching 197.75 lakh tonnes during 2024–25. Marine product exports reached all time high to ₹73,890 crore in 2025–26, despite challenges in global trade, reflecting the sector’s growing contribution to export earnings, employment generation and the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers
Ornamental fisheries is a specialised and high-value segment of the fisheries sector encompassing fish breeding and rearing, broodstock and seed production, live feed, aquatic plants, aquarium accessories, feed and health products, retailing, transportation and exports. India possesses rich ornamental fish biodiversity, with more than 374 indigenous freshwater ornamental fish species and over 700 indigenous marine ornamental fish species.
Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), 2,672 ornamental fish rearing and integrated breeding and rearing units have been approved across the country, comprising 2,465 rearing units and 207 integrated units. In addition, five freshwater ornamental fish brood banks and 144 recreational fisheries units were approved up to 2024–25, with a total approved investment of ₹230.45 crore.
As reported by ICAR-Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture, the Indian ornamental fish industry is estimated to be worth approximately ₹3,000 crore, including ornamental fish breeding, rearing and trade, aquarium accessories, aquatic plants and decorative products. The sector has considerable potential to support small-scale enterprises, women’s Self-Help Groups, rural youth, start-ups and other entrepreneurs because it can be undertaken with relatively limited land and water resources.
According to the latest complete annual data published by the Marine Products Export Development Authority, India exported approximately 59.73 tonnes of ornamental fish products valued at ₹16.94 crore during 2024–25. While India possesses extensive freshwater and marine ornamental fish diversity, the country has considerable scope to expand exports through commercial breeding of high-value species, promotion of indigenous varieties, improved quality assurance, certification, traceability, biosecurity and efficient live-fish logistics.

The Union Finance Minister highlighted India’s strong macroeconomic fundamentals, growth prospects and ongoing policy reforms, and encouraged greater investment by Singapore-based institutional investors and businesses in India’s growth story. Select infrastructure projects from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) pipeline were highlighted for consideration by investors, with a view to facilitating follow-up discussions and engagement with relevant Indian authorities.

Opportunities relating to aircraft leasing, treasury centres and greater participation by global investors in India’s financial markets were also explored. Mobilising long-term institutional capital and expanding avenues for financing India’s infrastructure and development priorities were key themes of the investment discussions. Smt. The participants reaffirmed their strong commitment to the Indian market and expressed their intention to sustain and expand their investments in India, reflecting continued confidence in the country’s long-term growth prospects.

Singapore expressed its keenness to share its experience in asset tokenisation. The discussions provided an opportunity to explore further cooperation between the financial authorities of the two countries on emerging technologies and their application in financial markets.

The visit reaffirmed the depth of the India–Singapore partnership and the shared interest in translating ongoing policy dialogue into greater investment, business engagement and financial cooperation. The wide-ranging interactions with Singapore’s political leadership, institutional investors, financial institutions and businesses helped showcase India’s growth and investment opportunities, identify areas of mutual interest and strengthen channels for follow-up engagement. The discussions are expected to support continued efforts to mobilise long-term capital, deepen financial connectivity and advance cooperation in emerging and strategic sectors.

title: Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda lays foundation stone of ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong
subtitle:
Dedicated research centre to strengthen preventive healthcare and address unique health challenges of Himalayan communities: Shri Nadda

“ICMR, Armed Forces Medical Services and AIIMS Bilaspur to join hands for high-altitude health research”

ICMR–Armed Forces collaboration to develop effective medical solutions for extreme-altitude conditions: Union MoS Shri Sanjay Seth

New research facility at Keylong to benefit Himalayan communities across India and beyond: Shri Jai Ram Thakur

High-altitude research initiative marks significant step towards better healthcare in remote Himalayan regions: Ms. Kangana Ranaut

Centre to build India’s own scientific evidence on Himalayan health; joint research to focus on soldiers and border communities

Research to explore drone-enabled medicine delivery, digital health and artificial intelligence to improve healthcare access in remote areas
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today performed the Bhumi Pujan and laid the foundation stone of the ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong, Himachal Pradesh. He expressed confidence that the Centre would establish a strong institutional foundation for high-altitude health research and advance scientific understanding of the unique health challenges faced by people living in the Himalayan region and personnel serving in high-altitude areas.
Addressing on the occasion, Union Minister Shri Nadda emphasised the importance of dedicated scientific research to understand the health implications of low oxygen levels, extreme cold, changing climatic conditions and the distinctive lifestyles of tribal communities. He highlighted the need for systematic studies of these region-specific challenges to identify health risks, develop appropriate interventions and strengthen preventive healthcare.
Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of strengthening healthcare infrastructure and ensuring access to quality healthcare, Shri Nadda said that the establishment of the Centre reflects the importance accorded to addressing the distinct healthcare needs of people living in remote Himalayan and border regions. He emphasised that research-based interventions would help improve health outcomes and enhance the well-being of local communities and Armed Forces personnel serving in these challenging environments.
Shri Nadda appreciated the collaboration between ICMR and the Armed Forces Medical Services in establishing the Centre. He also acknowledged the contribution of AIIMS Bilaspur, which would participate in studying the health impact of high-altitude conditions on patients visiting the region. The collaboration would bring together scientific expertise and clinical experience to deepen understanding of high-altitude health challenges and support evidence-based healthcare interventions.
Emphasising the long-term significance of the initiative, Shri Nadda said that the Centre would contribute to improving healthcare for tribal communities and Armed Forces personnel deployed in high-altitude areas. The research undertaken would support the development of appropriate preventive and promotive healthcare strategies, helping address the distinctive medical challenges associated with extreme environmental conditions and strengthening health services in the Himalayan region. Shri Nadda also appreciated ICMR’s role in developing the COVID-19 vaccine, which helped fight the pandemic not only in India but also in other countries around the world.
Union Minister of State for Defence Shri Sanjay Seth, who graced the occasion as Guest of Honour, highlighted the significance of the collaboration between the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Armed Forces Medical Services in establishing the High Altitude Research Centre at Keylong. Drawing on the Armed Forces’ experience of operating in high-altitude environments, he expressed confidence that the joint research initiative would help deepen scientific understanding of the health challenges associated with extreme altitudes and contribute to the development of effective medical solutions.
MoS Shri Seth emphasised the importance of combining ICMR’s scientific research capabilities with the practical experience of the Armed Forces Medical Services to address the health challenges posed by high-altitude conditions. The research undertaken at the centre is expected to support better understanding of the effects of altitude on the human body, with potential benefits for personnel serving in challenging environments as well as local communities living in the high-altitude regions of Himachal Pradesh.
Shri Jai Ram Thakur, Leader of Opposition in the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly and former Chief Minister, said that the establishment of the ICMR High Altitude Research Centre in Keylong is a significant step towards understanding the unique health challenges faced by people living in high-altitude regions. He emphasised that research into the effects of extreme cold, low oxygen levels and difficult geographical conditions would help develop better healthcare solutions, benefiting not only the people of Himachal Pradesh but also high-altitude communities across India and the world.
Ms. Kangana Ranaut, Member of Parliament from Mandi, said that improved connectivity has transformed life in the remote regions of Himachal Pradesh, which were once isolated for several months due to difficult geographical conditions. She highlighted that the establishment of the ICMR High Altitude Research Centre in the mountains of Keylong is a historic step that will advance scientific research, improve understanding of health challenges in high-altitude regions and contribute to the well-being of people in Himachal Pradesh and humanity at large.
Outlining the Centre's scientific vision, Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, ICMR, said, Keylong will be a place where the laboratory and the community meet, where local people are partners in research and where the goal is better health, not just research papers. He stressed on the important contribution of Armed Forces Medical Services, Himachal Pradesh Government and local community for the ICMR Centre.
Highlighting the impact of research, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, DGFMS said that the research undertaken at the Centre would directly strengthen medical care for soldiers deployed in some of the most demanding high-altitude terrain in the world. Combining the AFMS field experience with ICMR’s scientific expertise would help turn research findings into practical protocols for acclimatisation, early detection and treatment. He added that the knowledge generated at Keylong would benefit not only Armed Forces personnel but also the local communities who share these challenging environments.
Shri Ravi Thakur, former MLA from Lahaul & Spiti expressed confidence that research carried out at Keylong would lead to better healthcare and preventive measures for communities across these neighbouring Himalayan regions.
On this occasion, Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda and other dignitaries planted native Himalayan saplings under the Green ICMR Campus Initiative. Shri Nadda inaugurated a scientific exhibition for school students, launched the Centre’s website and institutional video, and released a commemorative postal special cover, marking key milestones in the establishment of the ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research at Keylong.
The Ceremony was participated by senior officers of the Armed Forces Medical Services and the Indian Air Force, scientists, Panchayati Raj representatives and local residents also attended the event.
Built on the foundation of the field station ICMR set up at Keylong nearly a decade ago, the Centre will be a permanent, year-round institution with state-of-the-art laboratories and specialised human resources. Its central mandate will be to generate evidence on the health effects of high altitude, low oxygen levels, extreme cold and changing climatic conditions. A key feature will be collaboration between ICMR, the Armed Forces Medical Services and other research institutions, bringing together expertise in biomedical research, public health and high-altitude physiology. Thus, the Centre will undertake research relevant to both the Armed Forces and civilian populations, with a focus on altitude-related health risks, acclimatisation, maternal and newborn health, child growth and nutrition, and disease patterns in Himalayan communities. It will also examine how emerging technologies, including drone-enabled medicine delivery, digital health and artificial intelligence, can improve access to healthcare in remote and difficult-to-reach areas. The resulting evidence is expected to inform healthcare practices, strengthen preventive and clinical approaches for personnel deployed at high altitude, and support better health services for communities living in India's Himalayan and border regions, including Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Centre Urges States/UTs to Ensure Prominent Display of Healthcare Service Rates at Clinical Establishments
subtitle:
Union Health Secretary writes to Chief Secretaries of all States and UTs, calling for effective implementation of provisions relating to transparent display of healthcare charges

Move aims to empower patients to make informed healthcare decisions, prevent billing-related disputes and strengthen trust in healthcare services

States/UTs also urged to facilitate transparent display of package rates for international patients visiting India on Medical and Ayush Visas
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 1:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening transparency, accountability and patient-centric healthcare delivery, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has urged all States and Union Territories (UTs) to ensure the prominent display of rates charged for services and facilities offered by Clinical Establishments.
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, in a letter to the Chief Secretaries of all States and UTs, has called for a review of compliance with applicable regulatory provisions and appropriate measures to ensure that information on healthcare service charges is clearly visible and easily accessible to patients and their attendants.
Emphasising the importance of transparency in healthcare pricing, the Union Health Secretary noted that the conspicuous display of rates would help patients and their families understand the likely cost of treatment, make informed healthcare decisions and plan their medical expenditure. Greater transparency would also help minimise avoidable confusion and billing-related disputes, while fostering trust and confidence in the healthcare delivery system.
The letter refers to the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, and the Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules, 2012, which provide a regulatory framework for Clinical Establishments. Under the Rules, Clinical Establishments in States and UTs where the Act is applicable are required to display the rates charged for each type of service provided and facilities available at a conspicuous place, in the local language as well as in English, for the benefit of patients and their attendants.
In States and UTs where the Act is not applicable, Clinical Establishments are regulated under the respective State/UT frameworks, several of which also contain provisions relating to the display of rates for healthcare services and facilities.
Recognising that health is a State subject and that implementation and enforcement of the applicable regulatory provisions rest with the respective States and UTs, the Union Health Secretary has called upon the Chief Secretaries to ensure effective compliance through the authorities concerned.
The letter also places particular emphasis on transparency in healthcare pricing for international patients. States and UTs have been requested to encourage the prominent display, wherever applicable, of package rates offered to foreign patients travelling to India on Medical or Ayush Visas. This would enable international patients to make informed choices, help minimise pricing and billing-related grievances and further strengthen India's position as a trusted destination for medical and Ayush care.
The Union Health Secretary has sought the personal attention of the Chief Secretaries in this matter and requested them to issue appropriate advisories to the concerned authorities and Clinical Establishments for necessary action, including ensuring that rates are displayed at conspicuous, clearly visible and easily accessible locations, in accordance with applicable regulations.
The initiative reinforces the Government of India's commitment to making healthcare delivery more transparent, accountable and responsive to patients' needs, ensuring that access to clear information on healthcare charges becomes an integral part of patient-centric care.

content:
Union Minister of Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy today launched the Commercialisation Catalogue of Technologies developed under the Science & Technology (S&T) Programme of the Ministry of Mines, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Department of Science and Technology (DST), and industry-sponsored programmes. This is an important step towards bridging the gap between research and industries showcasing indigenous technologies and facilitating their transfer, adoption, and commercialisation by industry.
The initiative aims to systematically document, showcase and promote technologies developed through publicly funded research and industry-supported projects, facilitating their adoption by industries, technology transfer, licensing and commercialisation. The proposed Catalogue seeks to address this gap by bringing verified technical information on such technologies together in a single, accessible repository for industries and prospective technology adopters.

https://research.mines.gov.in/

title: NHAI Introduces Stricter Monitoring to Ensure Clean and Well-Maintained Toilets Blocks and other Facilities at Toll Plazas
subtitle: User Fee Collection Agencies may be barred from NHAI bids for 15 days or until all pending deficiencies are rectified
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of its continued efforts to improve cleanliness and maintenance of toilet facilities along National Highways, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has introduced a stricter monitoring and enforcement mechanism. The new measures will ensure proper upkeep and maintenance of toilet blocks and other facilities, including toll collection booths, surrounding areas and signboards. The citizen-centric initiative also aims to ensure that agencies responsible for maintaining public-facing infrastructure meet prescribed service standards and address deficiencies promptly.
User Fee Collection Agencies will be required to comply with the prescribed service standards for toilets and other facilities. Under the new mechanism, NHAI officials will inspect these facilities at least once every week. If any deficiency is found, the concerned User Fee Collection Agency will be issued a show-cause notice and directed to rectify the issue within the stipulated time.
To ensure transparency and proper monitoring, notices along with dated photographs will be uploaded on NHAI’s Data Lake portal. The concerned agency will also be required to submit its reply and upload photographs showing the corrective action taken. NHAI field units will monitor progress and ensure that deficiencies are addressed within the prescribed time.
Penalties for non-compliance
Where a deficiency amounts to a violation of the contract or prescribed service standards, NHAI will impose the applicable penalty in accordance with the contractual provisions and existing guidelines.
NHAI has also introduced a provision to take action against agencies that repeatedly fail to rectify deficiencies. If the number of notices for unresolved deficiencies reaches or exceeds 10% of the total number of toll plazas being operated by an agency, the agency will be declared a
non-performer
. Such an agency will not be eligible to participate in bidding for toll plazas, regular toll plaza contracts, civil works or any other NHAI bid for a period of 15 days or until all pending deficiencies are rectified.
The new mechanism will apply to publicly funded toll plazas and other toll plazas where User Fee Collection Agencies are appointed by NHAI. It will operate in addition to the existing policies, guidelines and contractual provisions.
National Highway Users at the Core of Facilities
In 2025, NHAI launched its citizen-centric initiative, the
‘Clean Toilet Picture Challenge’
.
The unique initiative encourages National Highway users to report unclean toilet facilities at the toll plazas by uploading clear, geo-tagged, and time-stamped photographs through the
Rajmargyatra
Mobile App. Each eligible vehicle registration number reporting such an instance receives a reward of Rs. 1,000 (Rupees One Thousand) in the form of a FASTag recharge.
Through ‘
Clean Toilet Picture Challenge’
and strengthening of the monitoring framework, NHAI is adopting a multi-pronged approach towards improving toilet facilities along National Highways. The approach combines public participation, regular inspections, digital documentation and time-bound corrective action to improve service delivery and ensure accountability among agencies responsible for maintaining these facilities.
By enabling citizens to report deficiencies and strengthening oversight of service providers, NHAI aims to promote cleaner, better-maintained toilet facilities and provide an enhanced traveling experience for National Highway users.

content:
In a significant step towards strengthening rural entrepreneurship and promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities, the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Academy of RUDSETI (NAR) to establish uniform training standards, ensure quality administration and facilitate systematic capacity building across Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) in the country.
The MoU exchange took place on 12 October 2026 in the presence of Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development. The MoU was exchanged between Shri S. Sasikumar, Joint Secretary (Rural Skills), Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development, and Shri Raju N. Kori, Director General, National Academy of RUDSETI (NAR).
A key focus of the partnership will be to improve candidate registration through Kaushal Panjee and Aadhaar-based face authentication through the Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS), while enhancing the quality and relevance of training delivered through RSETIs. This will include the implementation of National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)-aligned new-age courses, the adoption of industry-benchmarked training aids and equipment, and the delivery of core Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) courses as notified by MoRD. The partnership will also strengthen Training of Trainers (ToT), assessment and certification of trainees and trainers through the Unified Portal (kaushal.rural.gov.in), and compliance with the Common Norms notified by the Ministry.
A training target of 6.35 lakh rural youth is given to RSETIs for the current year, comprising women, SC/ST, PwD and other vulnerable groups which is more than the training target fixed for the previous year, 2025–26.
The MoU marks an important step towards strengthening the RSETI ecosystem through improved training quality, institutional capacity, digital governance and outcome-oriented monitoring. By reinforcing the link between skill development, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods, the partnership seeks to enhance the capacity of rural youth to establish viable enterprises and contribute to inclusive rural economic growth.
The MoU marks an important step towards reinforcing the RSETI ecosystem and strengthening its role in rural skill development, entrepreneurship promotion and livelihood generation. The initiative aligns with the broader objectives of the Ministry of Rural Development to empower rural communities through skill development, enterprise creation and sustainable livelihoods, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, participated in the 8th India–UK Science and Innovation Council (SIC) Meeting with the Rt Hon Jonathan Reynolds, UK Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, at New Delhi.
The meeting reviewed progress in bilateral science and innovation cooperation and explored opportunities to strengthen research partnerships, emerging technology collaboration and the translation of scientific research into practical applications.
The Indian delegation included Prof. Ajay Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Prof. Umesh Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST); Dr. Rajesh Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT); Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences; Dr. Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, Chief Executive Officer, Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF); and Dr. Rajesh Pathak, Secretary, Technology Development Board (TDB), along with other senior officials from the concerned departments and institutions.
The UK delegation was led by the Rt Hon Jonathan Reynolds MP, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation and Trade, and included Ms. Lindy Cameron, British High Commissioner to India; Mr. Ben Mellor, Deputy High Commissioner to India; Ms. Amanda Brooks, Interim Permanent Secretary, Department for Business, Innovation and Trade; Mr. Harjinder Kang, His Majesty’s Trade Commissioner; and Mr. Rhys Bowen, International Director, Department for Business, Innovation and Trade, along with other representatives of the UK’s science, research and innovation ecosystem.
On the occasion, Dr. Jitendra Singh and Jonathan Reynolds jointly inaugurated the BRIC-CDFD–ONT India Genomics Centre of Excellence. The inauguration was attended by Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology and Director General, Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council (BRIC); Prof. Ullas Kolthur-Seetharam, Director, BRIC-CDFD; and Mr. Nick Keher, Chief Financial Officer, Oxford Nanopore Technologies.
The Council’s broader cooperation agenda builds on the India–UK Research and Innovation Memorandum of Understanding, the Technology Security Initiative and India–UK Vision 2035. These frameworks provide a foundation for collaboration among research institutions, universities, industry and innovators, with a focus on scientific advancement and translating research into technologies and applications.
Industry-led research and technology commercialisation remain important areas of engagement. The Department of Science and Technology’s collaboration with Innovate UK supports joint industrial research and development projects aimed at developing new intellectual property, technologies, processes and prototypes. Eight projects have been agreed for support under the programme in areas including advanced manufacturing, power electronics and net-zero technologies, and are at various stages of implementation.
Cooperation also extends to emerging and strategic technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, quantum technologies, semiconductors, critical minerals, advanced materials, biotechnology, telecommunications and net-zero technologies. These areas offer opportunities to draw on complementary research capabilities, strengthen innovation ecosystems and support the development of technologies with industrial and societal applications.
Joint research between Indian and UK institutions also covers antimicrobial resistance, healthcare, agriculture, climate and weather science, geohazards, advanced manufacturing and fundamental science. Collaboration in weather and climate science includes research on natural hazards associated with the South Asian monsoon, improved modelling capabilities and risk-based forecasting.
The meeting reaffirmed the importance of sustained institutional engagement and closer links between research, industry and innovation ecosystems. Continued India–UK cooperation can help advance scientific discovery, strengthen research partnerships and translate scientific capabilities into practical solutions for shared challenges.

The Indian delegation was led by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh, and comprised Prof. Umesh Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST); and Dr. Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Adviser and Head, International Bilateral Cooperation, DST.
The UK delegation comprised Mr. Jonathan Reynolds MP, Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade; Ms. Lindy Cameron, British High Commissioner to India; and Ms. Amanda Brooks, Interim Permanent Secretary, Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s space-sector reforms had opened new opportunities for private industry, startups and technology developers, enabling established research institutions to focus on advanced research and technology development. Building on this experience, India and the UK can expand cooperation through research partnerships, technology development, investment and greater industry participation. Their longstanding relationship and complementary scientific capabilities provide a strong foundation for taking bilateral cooperation to the next level.
The discussions covered collaboration in space science, satellite development and research, along with stronger engagement between scientific institutions and technology enterprises in both countries. With around 800 space-technology startups in India, Dr. Jitendra Singh proposed greater connectivity between Indian and British startups and smaller companies to facilitate innovation, strengthen supply chains and expand commercial opportunities.

Drawing on the experience of opening up the space sector, India is creating avenues for wider participation in nuclear energy and technology development.

content:
The Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF), a flagship initiative of the Government of India, has announced the first cohort of 19 Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs), marking a significant milestone in the implementation of the ₹1 lakh crore Fund. The Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) in its meeting held on October 08, 2026 has approved 14 Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and 5 Focused Research Organisations (FROs), with a total RDIF commitment of ₹7,131 crore.
The ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme was launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in November 2025. The initiative reflects the Government's vision of transforming India from a technology consumer into a nation that develops globally competitive technologies and products and emerges as a leading  technology provider in the world.
The RDIF represents one of India's most ambitious and creative initiatives to transform its research and innovation ecosystem. By making long-term, patient capital available for high risk, high impact research and development, the Fund seeks to address a critical financing gap that has historically constrained private sector investment in emerging and strategic technologies.
The RDIF is being managed by an Independent Business Unit housed within the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. The first call for applications from prospective SLFMs was launched in January 2026. Applications received under the call underwent a rigorous, multi-stage evaluation process, including detailed objective assessment of applications and in-person interactions with an Expert Advisory Committee. Following this process, the proposals were placed before the Executive Council of ANRF and subsequently before the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) for consideration and approval.
The 19 institutions approved under the first cohort will play a pivotal role in channelling RDIF capital to Eligible Technology Enterprises (ETEs) undertaking research, development and innovation activities at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 and above. These SLFMs are expected to mobilise private capital equivalent to the RDIF contribution.
The operationalisation of the first cohort represents an important step towards advancing India's technological sovereignty, reducing dependence on imported technologies, and building a globally competitive, innovation-led economy. By fostering a robust ecosystem for private sector-led research and development in ‘Science 4 Technology’, the RDIF will be a pillar of India emerging as a global hub of technology development and innovation, in line with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047.
EGoS also approved additional five technologies for covering under the RDI Fund.
Building on this milestone, the RDIF will continue to invite applications and onboard additional cohorts of SLFMs in the near future, expanding the reach of the Fund and accelerating public – private partnership and investment in India's research, development and innovation ecosystem.

title: Large- and small-scale magnetic activity driving microwave polar brightening in the Sun
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Researchers have probed the mystery of why the poles of the Sun shine much brighter than the rest of the solar disk when mapped at certain specific microwave and radio frequencies.
The study could provide valuable insights into the magnetic field and temperature conditions in the Sun's polar atmosphere.
The Sun's polar regions play an important role in the evolution of its magnetic field and the generation of the solar wind. However, despite decades of observations, the cause of microwave polar brightening,
the enhanced radio emission seen near the Sun's poles, has remained unclear.
Microwave polar brightening appears as an increase in radio brightness near the Sun's poles.
Earlier studies have linked this brightening to features such as polar coronal holes, polar faculae, and magnetic fields.
Coronal holes are dark regions in EUV images where magnetic field lines are predominantly open, allowing the fast solar wind to escape. However, the contribution of each of these features and their role in the long-term behaviour of microwave polar brightening have not been fully understood.
In a recent study carried out through a collaboration of researchers from the Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES), Nainital, an autonomous research institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, Udaipur Solar Observatory (USO)/ Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), IIT Delhi and IIT Roorkee, a comprehensive investigation of microwave polar brightening was carried out using nearly three decades of observations from the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NoRH) operating at 17 GHz.
The radio data were combined with extreme-ultraviolet observations from NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory and magnetic field measurements from the Wilcox Solar Observatory to investigate the origin and long-term evolution of this phenomenon.
Fig 1:
Long-term evolution of microwave polar brightening and polar coronal hole area at the north and south poles derived from Nobeyama Radioheliograph observations. The observations reveal clear solar-cycle variation and hemispheric asymmetry.
The research team, led by Mr. Rohan Bose, a DST INSPIRE Senior Research Fellow affiliated with ARIES, Nainital, and IIT Roorkee, along with Dr. Anshu Kumari (USO/PRL), Dr. Vaibhav Pant (IIT Delhi), and other collaborators, revealed a a clear north–south difference in the long-term evolution of microwave polar brightening and the area of polar coronal holes.
To understand the role of coronal holes, the researchers compared microwave observations with the areas of polar coronal holes identified from extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) images. The study found a strong relationship between microwave polar brightening and the size of polar coronal holes. An even stronger relationship was observed between microwave polar brightening and the strength of the Sun's polar magnetic field. These findings show that the long-term changes in microwave polar brightening are closely connected to the magnetic structure of the Sun's polar atmosphere.
Fig 2:
Comparison of microwave polar brightening with polar coronal-hole area and polar magnetic-field strength. Strong correlations are observed between all three quantities.
The researchers also examined individual microwave bright patches by comparing microwave observations with simultaneous extreme-ultraviolet images. They found that many of these bright regions coincide with small, bright features known as coronal bright points, which are formed by small-scale magnetic loops and are commonly found within polar coronal holes. In several cases, the bright regions were also linked to coronal jets, indicating continuous small-scale magnetic activity in the Sun's polar atmosphere.
Fig 3:
Examples of microwave bright patches observed within polar coronal holes. Many of these brightenings are associated with coronal bright points (left) and coronal jets (right) seen in extreme-ultraviolet observations.
The findings published in the Astrophysical Journal, indicate that both large-scale and small-scale magnetic processes influence microwave polar brightening. While the overall brightness variation tracks the evolution of the polar magnetic field and coronal holes, localized brightening is often associated with compact magnetic structures and jet activity within these regions. These findings provide strong observational evidence that microwave polar brightening is governed by the evolution of the Sun's polar magnetic environment and highlight the importance of radio observations for understanding solar polar activity and the origin of the solar wind.

title: Molecular geometry tweak opens new way for smart biomaterials
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Researchers have demonstrated how a remarkably small change in molecular structure can profoundly influence the way peptide-based molecules organize and function.
Such an approach could support the development of adaptable peptide-based nanomaterials for applications in biosensing, bioimaging, smart photonic materials, optoelectronics, and molecular electronics.
Peptides, the building blocks of proteins, can spontaneously organize into ordered nanostructures through supramolecular self-assembly. However, controlling this process to obtain desired structures and properties remains a major challenge.
A study by the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) found that by introducing just, a single methylene (–CH₂–) spacer between a peptide and a fluorescent pyrene unit, the researchers were able to alter molecular geometry and, consequently, the self-assembly behaviour of the system.
The research led by Dr. Goutam Ghosh at CeNS, Bengaluru, together with his PhD student Mr. Sourav Moyra, in collaboration with Mr. Tarak Nath Das (JNCASR, Bengaluru) and Dr. Rabindra Nath Manna (Ghatal Rabindra Satabarsiki Mahavidyalaya, West Bengal) showed that the subtle addition of one carbon atom changed the relative orientation of the molecular components. This led to distinctly different molecular packing, supramolecular chirality, fluorescence lifetime behaviour, and nanoscale organization—without changing the fundamental peptide framework.
Fig: Schematic representation of how a minute change in molecular structure tunes the self-assembly behaviour and material properties
The findings introduce a useful molecular design strategy for programming functional soft materials through controlled molecular organization rather than extensive chemical modification. The work was published in the journal Polymer Chemistry by Royal Society of Chemistry.
The work highlights how small molecular changes can provide powerful control over supramolecular organization and material function, offering new opportunities for the rational design of next-generation functional and responsive biomaterials.

title: TDB-DST signs agreement with Peptris for ₹86 crore RDI support to accelerate AI-driven drug discovery and development
subtitle: VIGOR programme to advance four AI-discovered drug candidates towards clinical development, strengthening India’s pharmaceutical innovation ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 OCT 2026 10:52AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards accelerating the development of next-generation therapeutics through artificial intelligence, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with Peptris Technologies Private Limited, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹86 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
The project, titled VIGOR: Advancing AI-Discovered Molecules from Bench to Clinic, has a total project cost of ₹172 crore. It aims to advance four drug candidates from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-6 through preclinical development, validation and preparation for clinical trials. The financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
Artificial intelligence is opening new possibilities in drug discovery by enabling researchers to identify promising molecules, investigate disease mechanisms and accelerate the search for potential therapies. However, translating computational discoveries into viable drug candidates requires extensive experimental validation, preclinical studies and clinical development.
Peptris’ VIGOR programme seeks to address this critical transition by leveraging its proprietary AI-driven drug discovery platform to advance a portfolio of molecules towards clinical development. The programme focuses on therapeutic areas with significant unmet medical needs, with an emphasis on identifying and developing novel therapies through a combination of computational capabilities, scientific validation and established drug-development processes.
The programme covers four drug candidates: PEPR111, targeting neuromuscular disorders and oncology; PEPRX101, focused on alopecia; PEPR202, targeting neuropathy; and PEPR112, focused on DMD. Each candidate is currently positioned at TRL-4, with the project targeting advancement to TRL-6. The development programme envisages a structured progression over three years, encompassing advanced preclinical and investigational new drug (IND)-enabling studies, formulation development, clinical trial preparation and initiation activities, subject to the relevant scientific and regulatory requirements.
The VIGOR programme is designed to build on Peptris’ AI-based drug discovery capabilities and its existing platform experience to accelerate the development of novel therapeutic candidates. The approach combines AI-enabled discovery with established drug-development expertise, including the use of global contract research organisation (CRO) networks to support development and validation. By supporting the advancement of multiple candidates within a coordinated programme, the project seeks to strengthen the translation of AI-led research into potential therapeutic products. Its focus on selected disease areas also reflects the opportunity to direct innovation towards conditions where effective treatment options remain limited.
Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said,
“The application of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical research has the potential to transform how new drug candidates are identified and developed. However, translating promising discoveries into validated therapeutic candidates requires sustained investment, rigorous scientific evaluation and a structured development pathway. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting such technology-intensive programmes to help bridge the gap between innovation and clinical development, while strengthening India’s capabilities in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and AI-led healthcare innovation.”
Representative of Peptris Technologies Private Limited said,
“The support from TDB under the RDI Fund will help us advance our VIGOR programme and progress our AI-discovered molecules through critical preclinical development milestones. Our approach combines AI-driven discovery with experimental validation and established drug-development processes to address unmet medical needs. This partnership will support our efforts to translate promising computational discoveries into therapeutic candidates with the potential to progress towards clinical development.”
